title.zh: 卷四四 列傳第三六 儒林
title.raw: 卷四四 列傳第三六 儒林 Volume 44 Biographies 36: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 班固稱「儒家者流，蓋出於司徒之官，助人君順陰陽，行教化」者也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said that "the Confucian school arose from the Minister of Education's office, aiding the ruler in harmonizing yin and yang and carrying out transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu said that "the Confucian school arose from the Minister of Education's office, aiding the ruler in harmonizing yin and yang and carrying out transformation."

sentences.zh: 聖人所以明天道，正人倫，是以古先哲王率由斯道。

translations.literal: The sage therefore illuminates Heaven's Way and rectifies human relations—thus the ancient sage-kings all followed this path.
translations.idiomatic: The sage therefore illuminates Heaven's Way and rectifies human relations—thus the ancient sage-kings all followed this path.

sentences.zh: 高祖生於邊朔，長於戎馬之間，因魏氏喪亂之餘，屬尒朱殘酷之舉，文章咸蕩，禮樂同奔，弦歌之音且絕，俎豆之容將盡。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was born on the frontier marches and grew up amid war-horses; because of the remnant disorders after the Northern Wei collapse, when Erzhu Rong's cruel measures fell upon the age, literature was swept away, rites and music fled together, the sound of string and song was nearly cut off, and the bearing of sacrificial vessels was almost exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was born on the frontier marches and grew up amid war-horses. After the Northern Wei fell into disorder and Erzhu Rong's cruel measures seized the age, literature was swept away and rites and music fled together; the sound of string and song was nearly cut off, and the bearing of sacrificial vessels was almost gone.

sentences.zh: 及仗義建旗，掃清區縣，以正君臣，以齊上下。

translations.literal: When he raised the banner of righteousness and swept the districts clean, he rectified ruler and subject and aligned superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: When he raised the banner of righteousness and swept the districts clean, he rectified ruler and subject and aligned superior and inferior.

sentences.zh: 至乎一人播越，九鼎潛移，文武神器，顧眄斯在，猶且援立宗支，重安社稷，豈非跼名教之地，漸仁義之風與？

translations.literal: When the One Man was cast adrift and the Nine Cauldrons shifted in secret, the vessels of civil and martial power—all turned their gaze here—yet he still supported a collateral branch of the house and again settled the altars of state. Was this not treading ground within the teaching of names, gradually entering the wind of humaneness and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: When the One Man was cast adrift and the Nine Cauldrons shifted in secret, the vessels of civil and martial power—all turned their gaze here—yet he still supported a collateral branch of the house and again settled the altars of state. Was this not treading ground within the teaching of names, gradually entering the wind of humaneness and righteousness?

sentences.zh: 屬疆埸多虞，戎車歲駕，雖庠序之制有所未遑，而儒雅之道遽形心慮。

translations.literal: Because the borders had many alarms and war-chariots went forth year by year, though the system of schools had not yet been attended to, the way of classical elegance took sudden shape in his heart and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Because the borders had many alarms and war-chariots went forth year by year, though the system of schools had not yet been attended to, the way of classical elegance took sudden shape in his heart and thought.

sentences.zh: 魏天平中，范陽盧景裕同從兄禮於本郡起逆，高祖免其罪，置之賓館，以經教授太原公以下。

translations.literal: In the Northern Wei Tianping era, Fanyang Lu Jingyu together with his elder cousin's son Li raised rebellion in their native commandery; Gao Huan pardoned their crimes and placed them in the guest lodge, using the classics to instruct the Prince of Taiyuan and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Northern Wei Tianping era, Fanyang Lu Jingyu together with his elder cousin's son Li raised rebellion in their native commandery. Gao Huan pardoned their crimes and placed them in the guest lodge, using the classics to instruct the Prince of Taiyuan and those below him.

sentences.zh: 及景裕卒，又以趙郡李同軌繼之。

translations.literal: When Jingyu died, Zhao commandery Li Tonggui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyu died, Zhao commandery Li Tonggui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 二賢並大蒙恩遇，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Both worthies received great favor and were treated with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Both worthies received great favor and were treated with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 同軌之亡，復徵中山張雕、渤海李鉉、刁柔、中山石曜等遞為諸子師友。

translations.literal: When Tonggui died, Zhongshan Zhang Diao, Bohai Li Xuan, Diao Rou, Zhongshan Shi Yao, and others were summoned in turn to serve as teachers and friends to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Tonggui died, Zhongshan Zhang Diao, Bohai Li Xuan, Diao Rou, Zhongshan Shi Yao, and others were summoned in turn to serve as teachers and friends to the princes.

sentences.zh: 及天保、大寧、武平之朝，亦引進名儒，授皇太子諸王經術。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao, Daning, and Wuping reigns as well, famous Confucians were brought in to teach the classics to the crown prince and the princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao, Daning, and Wuping reigns as well, famous Confucians were brought in to teach the classics to the crown prince and the princes.

sentences.zh: 然爰自始基，暨於季世，唯濟南之在儲宮，性識聰敏，頗自砥礪，以成其美。

translations.literal: Yet from the founding down to the final age, only Gao Yan of Jinan while in the Eastern Palace was clever and keen by nature and quite polished himself, thereby completing his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the founding down to the final age, only Gao Yan of Jinan while in the Eastern Palace was clever and keen by nature and quite polished himself, thereby completing his excellence.

sentences.zh: 自餘多驕恣傲狠，動違禮度，日就月將，無聞焉爾。

translations.literal: The rest were mostly arrogant, willful, and fierce; day by day they moved against ritual measure, and month by month there was nothing to be heard of improvement.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were mostly arrogant, willful, and fierce; day by day they moved against ritual measure, and month by month there was nothing to be heard of improvement.

sentences.zh: 鏤冰雕朽，迄用無成，蓋有由也。

translations.literal: Carving ice and sculpting rotten wood, in the end nothing was achieved—there was reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Carving ice and sculpting rotten wood, in the end nothing was achieved—there was reason for it.

sentences.zh: 夫帝子王孫，稟性淫逸，況義方之情不篤，邪僻之路競開，自非得自生知，體包上智，而內有聲色之娛，外多犬馬之好，安能入便篤行，出則友賢者也。

translations.literal: The emperor's sons and the king's grandsons are endowed with dissolute natures; moreover, when the force of moral instruction is not deep and paths of depravity compete to open, unless one is born with innate knowledge and one's person embraces supreme wisdom, while within there is the pleasure of sound and color and without there is fondness for dogs and horses—how can one enter and practice steadfast conduct, or go out and befriend the worthy?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's sons and the king's grandsons are endowed with dissolute natures. When the force of moral instruction is not deep and paths of depravity compete to open, unless one is born with innate knowledge and one's person embraces supreme wisdom, while within there is the pleasure of sound and color and without there is fondness for dogs and horses—how can one enter and practice steadfast conduct, or go out and befriend the worthy?

sentences.zh: 徒有師傅之資，終無琢磨之實。

translations.literal: They had only the qualifications of teachers and tutors, yet in the end no reality of polishing.
translations.idiomatic: They had only the qualifications of teachers and tutors, yet in the end no reality of polishing.

sentences.zh: 下之從化，如風靡草，是以世胄之門，罕聞強學。

translations.literal: Those below followed transformation like wind bending grass—thus among houses of hereditary nobility one rarely heard of strenuous study.
translations.idiomatic: Those below followed transformation like wind bending grass—thus among houses of hereditary nobility one rarely heard of strenuous study.

sentences.zh: 若使貴遊之輩，飾以明經，可謂稽山竹箭，加之以括羽，俯拾青紫，斷可知焉。

translations.literal: If the noble wanderers were adorned with mastery of the classics, it could be called bamboo arrows from Ji Hill with feathered shafts added—bowing to pick up purple and crimson rank, one could know it at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: If the noble wanderers were adorned with mastery of the classics, it could be called bamboo arrows from Ji Hill with feathered shafts added—bowing to pick up purple and crimson rank, one could know it at a glance.

sentences.zh: 而齊氏司存，或失其守，師保疑丞，皆賞勳舊，國學博士，徒有虛名，唯國子一學，生徒數十人耳，欲求官正國治，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Yet Qi offices in charge sometimes lost their posts; mentors, protectors, tutors, and aides were all rewarded for old merit, and doctorate lecturers in the National University had only empty names—only the single National University school had several tens of students. To seek upright officials and a well-governed state, was that possible?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi offices in charge sometimes lost their posts; mentors, protectors, tutors, and aides were all rewarded for old merit, and doctorate lecturers in the National University had only empty names—only the single National University school had several tens of students. To seek upright officials and a well-governed state, was that possible?

sentences.zh: 胄子以通經仕者唯博陵崔子發、廣平宋遊卿而已，自外莫見其人。

translations.literal: Among scions who entered office through mastery of the classics there were only Boling Cui Zifa and Guangping Song Youqing; beyond them no such men were seen.
translations.idiomatic: Among scions who entered office through mastery of the classics there were only Boling Cui Zifa and Guangping Song Youqing; beyond them no such men were seen.

sentences.zh: 幸朝章寬簡，政網疏闊，遊手浮惰，十室而九。

translations.literal: Fortunately court regulations were broad and simple and the governmental net sparse and loose; idlers floating in indolence filled nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately court regulations were broad and simple and the governmental net sparse and loose; idlers floating in indolence filled nine houses in ten.

sentences.zh: 故橫經受業之侶，遍於鄉邑；

translations.literal: Therefore companions who spread the classics and received instruction were everywhere in town and countryside;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore companions who spread the classics and received instruction were everywhere in town and countryside;

sentences.zh: 負笈從宦之徒，不遠千里。

translations.literal: those who bore satchels and followed office did not shrink from a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: those who bore satchels and followed office did not shrink from a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 伏膺無怠，善誘不倦。

translations.literal: They embraced learning without slackening and guided others tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced learning without slackening and guided others tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 入閭里之內，乞食為資；

translations.literal: Entering within hamlets and lanes, they took begging for food as their support;
translations.idiomatic: Entering within hamlets and lanes, they took begging for food as their support;

sentences.zh: 憩桑梓之陰，動逾千數。

translations.literal: resting in the shade of their native mulberry trees, they moved in numbers exceeding a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: resting in the shade of their native mulberry trees, they moved in numbers exceeding a thousand.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙之俗，此衆尤甚。

translations.literal: Among the customs of Yan and Zhao, this crowd was especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Among the customs of Yan and Zhao, this crowd was especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 齊制：諸郡並立學，置博士助教授經，學生俱差逼充員，士流及豪富之家皆不從調。

translations.literal: Qi regulations: every commandery established a school, set doctorate assistants to teach the classics, and students were all forcibly pressed to fill quotas; the scholar-gentry and powerful rich households all refused assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Qi regulations: every commandery established a school, set doctorate assistants to teach the classics, and students were all forcibly pressed to fill quotas; the scholar-gentry and powerful rich households all refused assignment.

sentences.zh: 備員旣非所好，墳籍固不關懷，又多被州郡官人驅使，縱有遊惰，亦不檢治，皆由上非所好之所致也。

translations.literal: Since filling quotas was not what they desired, tomb texts and records naturally did not concern them; moreover many were driven by commandery and prefecture officials—though there were idlers, no inspection was made. All stemmed from what those above did not favor.
translations.idiomatic: Since filling quotas was not what they desired, tomb texts and records naturally did not concern them; moreover many were driven by commandery and prefecture officials—though there were idlers, no inspection was made. All stemmed from what those above did not favor.

sentences.zh: 諸郡俱得察孝廉，其博士、助教及遊學之徒通經者，推擇充舉。

translations.literal: Every commandery could recommend Filial and Incorrupt candidates; among doctorate assistants, teaching assistants, and wandering students who had mastered the classics, the outstanding were chosen to fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery could recommend Filial and Incorrupt candidates; among doctorate assistants, teaching assistants, and wandering students who had mastered the classics, the outstanding were chosen to fill the quota.

sentences.zh: 射策十條，通八以上，聽九品出身，其尤異者亦蒙抽擢。

translations.literal: In the target-shooting examination of ten questions, those who passed eight or more were permitted entry at the ninth rank; the especially outstanding also received special promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the target-shooting examination of ten questions, those who passed eight or more were permitted entry at the ninth rank; the especially outstanding also received special promotion.

sentences.zh: 凡是經學諸生，多出自魏末大儒徐遵明門下。

translations.literal: Generally, students of classical learning mostly came from the school of Xu Zunming, the great Confucian of late Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, students of classical learning mostly came from the school of Xu Zunming, the great Confucian of late Wei.

sentences.zh: 河北講鄭康成所註《周易》。

translations.literal: North of the Yellow River they lectured on Zheng Xuan's commentary to the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River they lectured on Zheng Xuan's commentary to the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 遵明以傳盧景裕及清河崔瑾，景裕傳權會，權會傳郭茂。

translations.literal: Zunming transmitted to Lu Jingyu of Qinghe and Cui Jin; Jingyu transmitted to Quan Hui; Hui transmitted to Guo Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming transmitted to Lu Jingyu of Qinghe and Cui Jin; Jingyu transmitted to Quan Hui; Hui transmitted to Guo Mao.

sentences.zh: 權會早入京都，郭茂恒在門下教授。

translations.literal: Hui entered the capital early; Guo Mao constantly taught at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hui entered the capital early; Guo Mao constantly taught at the gate.

sentences.zh: 其後能言《易》者多出郭茂之門。

translations.literal: Afterward those who could discourse on the Book of Changes mostly came from Guo Mao's school.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward those who could discourse on the Book of Changes mostly came from Guo Mao's school.

sentences.zh: 河南及青、齊之間，儒生多講王輔嗣所註《周易》，師訓蓋寡。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River and in Qing and Qi, Confucian students mostly lectured on Wang Fusi's commentary to the Book of Changes; teacherly instruction was quite sparse.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River and in Qing and Qi, Confucian students mostly lectured on Wang Fusi's commentary to the Book of Changes; teacherly instruction was quite sparse.

sentences.zh: 齊時儒士，罕傳《尚書》之業，徐遵明兼通之。

translations.literal: Among Qi Confucians, few transmitted the study of the Book of Documents; Xu Zunming mastered it as well.
translations.idiomatic: Among Qi Confucians, few transmitted the study of the Book of Documents; Xu Zunming mastered it as well.

sentences.zh: 遵明受業於屯留王總，傳授浮陽李周仁及渤海張文敬及李鉉、權會，並鄭康成所注，非古文也。

translations.literal: Zunming received instruction from Tunliu Wang Zong and transmitted to Fuyang Li Zhouren, Bohai Zhang Wenjing, Li Xuan, and Quan Hui—all Zheng Xuan's commentary, not the ancient text version.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming received instruction from Tunliu Wang Zong and transmitted to Fuyang Li Zhouren, Bohai Zhang Wenjing, Li Xuan, and Quan Hui—all Zheng Xuan's commentary, not the ancient text version.

sentences.zh: 下里諸生，略不見孔氏注解。

translations.literal: Students in the lower countryside scarcely saw Kong Anguo's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Students in the lower countryside scarcely saw Kong Anguo's commentary.

sentences.zh: 武平末，河間劉光伯、信都劉士元始得費甝《義疏》，乃留意焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping, Hejian Liu Guangbo and Xindu Liu Shiyuan first obtained Fei Kan's Expository Commentary and then gave it attention.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping, Hejian Liu Guangbo and Xindu Liu Shiyuan first obtained Fei Kan's Expository Commentary and then gave it attention.

sentences.zh: 其《詩》、《禮》、《春秋》尤為當時所尚，諸生多兼通之。

translations.literal: The Book of Odes, the Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were especially honored in the age; most students mastered more than one.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes, the Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were especially honored in the age; most students mastered more than one.

sentences.zh: 《三禮》並出遵明之門。

translations.literal: The Three Rites all came from Zunming's school.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rites all came from Zunming's school.

sentences.zh: 徐傳業於李鉉、沮俊、田元鳳、馮偉、紀顯敬、呂黃龍、夏懷敬。

translations.literal: Xu transmitted the profession to Li Xuan, Ju Jun, Tian Yuanfeng, Feng Wei, Ji Xianjing, Lü Huanglong, and Xia Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu transmitted the profession to Li Xuan, Ju Jun, Tian Yuanfeng, Feng Wei, Ji Xianjing, Lü Huanglong, and Xia Huaijing.

sentences.zh: 李鉉又傳授刁柔、張買奴、鮑季詳、邢峙、劉晝、熊安生。

translations.literal: Li Xuan again transmitted to Diao Rou, Zhang Mainu, Bao Jixiang, Xing Zhi, Liu Zhou, and Xiong Ansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan again transmitted to Diao Rou, Zhang Mainu, Bao Jixiang, Xing Zhi, Liu Zhou, and Xiong Ansheng.

sentences.zh: 安生又傳孫靈暉、郭仲堅、丁恃德。

translations.literal: Ansheng again transmitted to Sun Linghui, Guo Zhongjian, and Ding Side.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng again transmitted to Sun Linghui, Guo Zhongjian, and Ding Side.

sentences.zh: 其後生能通《禮經》者多是安生門人。

translations.literal: Afterward students who could master the Classic of Rites were mostly Ansheng's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward students who could master the Classic of Rites were mostly Ansheng's disciples.

sentences.zh: 諸生盡通《小戴禮》，於《周》、《儀禮》兼通者十二三焉。

translations.literal: Students all mastered the Elder Dai Rites; those who also mastered the Rites of Zhou and the Etiquette and Ritual were only one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Students all mastered the Elder Dai Rites; those who also mastered the Rites of Zhou and the Etiquette and Ritual were only one or two in ten.

sentences.zh: 通《毛詩》者多出於魏朝博陵劉獻之。

translations.literal: Those who mastered the Mao version of the Book of Odes mostly came from Liu Xianzhi of Boling in the Wei court.
translations.idiomatic: Those who mastered the Mao version of the Book of Odes mostly came from Liu Xianzhi of Boling in the Wei court.

sentences.zh: 獻之傳李周仁，周仁傳董令度、程歸則，歸則傳劉敬和、張思伯、劉軌思。

translations.literal: Xianzhi transmitted to Li Zhouren; Zhouren transmitted to Dong Lingdu and Cheng Guize; Guize transmitted to Liu Jinghe, Zhang Sibo, and Liu Guisi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi transmitted to Li Zhouren; Zhouren transmitted to Dong Lingdu and Cheng Guize; Guize transmitted to Liu Jinghe, Zhang Sibo, and Liu Guisi.

sentences.zh: 其後能言《詩》者多出二劉之門。

translations.literal: Afterward those who could discourse on the Book of Odes mostly came from the two Liu's schools.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward those who could discourse on the Book of Odes mostly came from the two Liu's schools.

sentences.zh: 河北諸儒能通《春秋》者，並服子慎所注，亦出徐生之門。

translations.literal: North of the Yellow River Confucians who mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals all followed Fu Qian's commentary and likewise came from Xu's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River Confucians who mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals all followed Fu Qian's commentary and likewise came from Xu's disciples.

sentences.zh: 張買奴、馬敬德、邢峙、張思伯、張雕、劉晝、鮑長暄、王元則並得服氏之精微。

translations.literal: Zhang Mainu, Ma Jingde, Xing Zhi, Zhang Sibo, Zhang Diao, Liu Zhou, Bao Changxuan, and Wang Yuanze all obtained the subtlety of Fu's school.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mainu, Ma Jingde, Xing Zhi, Zhang Sibo, Zhang Diao, Liu Zhou, Bao Changxuan, and Wang Yuanze all obtained the subtlety of Fu's school.

sentences.zh: 又有衛覬、陳達、潘叔度雖不傳徐氏之門，亦為通解。

translations.literal: There were also Wei Kan, Chen Da, and Pan Shudu who, though they did not transmit Xu Zunming's school, were thoroughly versed.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Wei Kan, Chen Da, and Pan Shudu who, though they did not transmit Xu Zunming's school, were thoroughly versed.

sentences.zh: 又有姚文安、秦道靜初亦學服氏，後更兼講杜元凱所注。

translations.literal: There were also Yao Wen'an and Qin Daojing who at first studied Fu's school and later also lectured on Du Yu's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Yao Wen'an and Qin Daojing who at first studied Fu's school and later also lectured on Du Yu's commentary.

sentences.zh: 其河外儒生俱伏膺杜氏。

translations.literal: Confucian students beyond the river all revered Du's school.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian students beyond the river all revered Du's school.

sentences.zh: 其《公羊》、《穀梁》二傳，儒者多不措懷。

translations.literal: The Gongyang and Guliang traditions—most Confucians paid them no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang and Guliang traditions—most Confucians paid them no heed.

sentences.zh: 《論語》、《孝經》，諸學徒莫不通講。

translations.literal: The Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety—all students lectured on them without exception.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety—all students lectured on them without exception.

sentences.zh: 諸儒如權會、李鉉、刁柔、熊安生、劉軌思、馬敬德之徒多自出義疏。

translations.literal: Confucians such as Quan Hui, Li Xuan, Diao Rou, Xiong Ansheng, Liu Guisi, Ma Jingde, and the like mostly produced their own expository commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians such as Quan Hui, Li Xuan, Diao Rou, Xiong Ansheng, Liu Guisi, Ma Jingde, and the like mostly produced their own expository commentaries.

sentences.zh: 雖曰專門，亦皆粗習也。

translations.literal: Though called specialists, all were only roughly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Though called specialists, all were only roughly practiced.

sentences.zh: 今序所錄諸生，或終於魏朝，或名宦不達，縱能名家，又闕其由來及所出郡國，並略存其姓名而已。

translations.literal: Now in the sequence recorded, some students ended in the Wei court or attained no fame in office; even if they could make a name for their school, their origins and native commanderies are missing—only their names are briefly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the sequence recorded, some students ended in the Wei court or attained no fame in office; even if they could make a name for their school, their origins and native commanderies are missing—only their names are briefly preserved.

sentences.zh: 俱取其尤通顯者列於《儒林》云。

translations.literal: All take the most thoroughly versed and illustrious and list them in Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: All take the most thoroughly versed and illustrious and list them in Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 熊安生名在周史，光伯、士元著於《隋書》，輒不重述。

translations.literal: Xiong Ansheng's name appears in Zhou history; Guangbo and Shiyuan are set forth in the History of Sui—here they are not repeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ansheng's name appears in Zhou history; Guangbo and Shiyuan are set forth in the History of Sui—here they are not repeated.

sentences.zh: 李鉉，字寶鼎，渤海南皮人也。

translations.literal: Li Xuan, styled Baoding, was a man of Nanpi in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan, styled Baoding, came from Nanpi in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 九歲入學，書《急就篇》，月餘便通。

translations.literal: At nine he entered school and copied the Rapid Writing Primer; in little more than a month he had mastered it.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he entered school and copied the Rapid Writing Primer; in little more than a month he had mastered it.

sentences.zh: 家素貧苦，常春夏務農，冬乃入學。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor; in spring and summer he always worked the fields, and only in winter entered school.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been poor; in spring and summer he always worked the fields, and only in winter entered school.

sentences.zh: 年十六，從浮陽李周仁受《毛詩》、《尚書》，章武劉子猛受《禮記》，常山房虬受《周官》《儀禮》，漁陽鮮于靈馥受《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: At sixteen he received the Mao version of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents from Fuyang Li Zhouren, the Record of Rites from Zhangwu Liu Zimeng, the Rites of Zhou and the Etiquette and Ritual from Changshan Fang Qiu, and the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals from Yuyang Xianyu Lingfu.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he received the Mao version of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents from Fuyang Li Zhouren, the Record of Rites from Zhangwu Liu Zimeng, the Rites of Zhou and the Etiquette and Ritual from Changshan Fang Qiu, and the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals from Yuyang Xianyu Lingfu.

sentences.zh: 鉉以鄉里無可師者，遂與州里楊元懿、河間宗惠振等結侶詣大儒徐遵明受業。

translations.literal: Because there was no teacher in his district, he joined Yang Yuanyi of the province and Zong Huizhen of Hejian and others as companions to go to the great Confucian Xu Zunming to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Because there was no teacher in his district, he joined Yang Yuanyi of the province and Zong Huizhen of Hejian and others as companions to go to the great Confucian Xu Zunming to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 居徐門下五年，常稱高第。

translations.literal: He dwelt five years at Xu's gate and was constantly called a top student.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt five years at Xu's gate and was constantly called a top student.

sentences.zh: 二十三，便自潛居，討論是非，撰定《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《三禮義疏》及《三傳異同》、《周易義例》，合三十餘卷。

translations.literal: At twenty-three he withdrew to seclusion, discussed right and wrong, and compiled expository commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao version of the Book of Odes, and the Three Rites, together with Divergences among the Three Traditions, and Patterns in the Meaning of the Book of Changes—in all more than thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three he withdrew to seclusion, discussed right and wrong, and compiled expository commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao version of the Book of Odes, and the Three Rites, together with Divergences among the Three Traditions and Patterns in the Meaning of the Book of Changes—in all more than thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 用心精苦，曾三冬不畜枕，每至睡時，假寐而已。

translations.literal: His mind was refined and bitterly strained; three winters he kept no pillow, and whenever sleep came he only dozed.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was refined and bitterly strained; three winters he kept no pillow, and whenever sleep came he only dozed.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，歸養二親，因教授鄉里，生徒恒至數百。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he returned to nourish both parents and thereby taught in his district; students constantly reached several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he returned to nourish both parents and thereby taught in his district; students constantly reached several hundred.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙間能言經者，多出其門。

translations.literal: Among Yan and Zhao, those who could discourse on the classics mostly came from his school.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yan and Zhao, those who could discourse on the classics mostly came from his school.

sentences.zh: 年三十六，丁父喪。

translations.literal: At thirty-six he mourned his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-six he mourned his father's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以鄉里寡文籍，來遊京師，讀所未見書。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, because his district had few texts, he came to wander the capital and read books he had not yet seen.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, because his district had few texts, he came to wander the capital and read books he had not yet seen.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，除太學博士。

translations.literal: The province recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; he was appointed doctorate lecturer in the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: The province recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; he was appointed doctorate lecturer in the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 武定中，李同軌卒後，高祖令世宗在京妙簡碩學，以教諸子。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, after Li Tonggui died, Gao Huan ordered Gao Cheng in the capital finely to select great scholars to teach the princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era, after Li Tonggui died, Gao Huan ordered Gao Cheng in the capital finely to select great scholars to teach the princes.

sentences.zh: 世宗以鉉應旨，徵詣晉陽。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng, because Xuan answered the intent, summoned him to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng, because Xuan answered the intent, summoned him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 時中山石曜、北平陽絢、北海王晞、清河崔瞻、廣平宋欽道及工書人韓毅同在東館，師友諸王。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongshan Shi Yao, Beiping Yang Xuan, Beihai Wang Xi, Qinghe Cui Zhan, Guangping Song Qindao, and the skilled calligrapher Han Yi were together in the Eastern Lodge, teachers and friends to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhongshan Shi Yao, Beiping Yang Xuan, Beihai Wang Xi, Qinghe Cui Zhan, Guangping Song Qindao, and the skilled calligrapher Han Yi were together in the Eastern Lodge, teachers and friends to the princes.

sentences.zh: 鉉以去聖久遠，文字多有乖謬，感孔子「必也正名」之言，乃喟然有刊正之意。

translations.literal: Xuan, because the sage had been distant for long and written characters had many errors, moved by Confucius's words "one must correct names," sighed with the intent to edit and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, because the sage had been distant for long and written characters had many errors, moved by Confucius's words "one must correct names," sighed with the intent to edit and correct.

sentences.zh: 於講授之暇，遂覽《說文》，爰及《倉》、《雅》，刪正六藝經注中謬字，名曰《字辨》。

translations.literal: In the intervals of lecturing he perused Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters, and also the Cang Jie and Erya, deleting and correcting mistaken characters in the annotated texts of the Six Classics, titled Character Discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of lecturing he perused Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters, and also the Cang Jie and Erya, deleting and correcting mistaken characters in the annotated texts of the Six Classics, titled Character Discrimination.

sentences.zh: 顯祖受禪，從駕還都。

translations.literal: When Gao Yang received the mandate he followed the imperial procession back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang received the mandate he followed the imperial procession back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天保初，詔鉉與殿中尚書邢卲、中書令魏收等參議禮律，仍兼國子博士。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao an edict ordered Xuan together with palace director Xing Shao, palace secretary Wei Shou, and others to deliberate on rites and statutes; he was concurrently doctorate lecturer in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao an edict ordered Xuan together with palace director Xing Shao, palace secretary Wei Shou, and others to deliberate on rites and statutes; he was concurrently doctorate lecturer in the National University.

sentences.zh: 時詔北平太守宋景業、西河太守綦毋懷文等草定新曆，錄尚書平原王高隆之令鉉與通直常侍房延佑、國子博士刁柔參考得失。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered Beiping administrator Song Jingye, Xihe administrator Qimu Huaiwen, and others to draft the new calendar; Recorder of the Masters of Writing Pingyuan Wang Gaolongzhi ordered Xuan together with direct-communication attendant Fang Yanyou and National University doctorate Diao Rou to examine gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict ordered Beiping administrator Song Jingye, Xihe administrator Qimu Huaiwen, and others to draft the new calendar; Recorder of the Masters of Writing Pingyuan Wang Gaolongzhi ordered Xuan together with direct-communication attendant Fang Yanyou and National University doctorate Diao Rou to examine gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 尋正國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made regular doctorate lecturer in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made regular doctorate lecturer in the National University.

sentences.zh: 廢帝之在東宮，顯祖詔鉉以經入授，甚見優禮。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign was in the Eastern Palace, Gao Yang edicted Xuan to enter and teach the classics; he received very generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign was in the Eastern Palace, Gao Yang edicted Xuan to enter and teach the classics; he received very generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 數年，病卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 特贈廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously enfeoffed as vice director of the court of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously enfeoffed as vice director of the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 及還葬故郡，太子致祭奠之禮，並使王人將送，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: When he was returned for burial in his native commandery, the crown prince sent rites of condolence and sacrifice, and also dispatched a royal envoy to escort the coffin—Confucians counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he was returned for burial in his native commandery, the crown prince sent rites of condolence and sacrifice, and also dispatched a royal envoy to escort the coffin—Confucians counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 楊元懿、宗惠振官亦俱至國子博士。

translations.literal: Yang Yuanyi and Zong Huizhen also both reached the post of National University doctorate lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanyi and Zong Huizhen also both reached the post of National University doctorate lecturer.

sentences.zh: 刁柔，字子溫，渤海人也。

translations.literal: Diao Rou, styled Ziwen, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Rou, styled Ziwen, came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父整，魏車騎將軍、贈司空。

translations.literal: His father Zheng was Northern Wei general of swift cavalry and posthumously enfeoffed as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng was Northern Wei general of swift cavalry and posthumously enfeoffed as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 柔少好學，綜習經史，尤留心禮儀。

translations.literal: Rou from youth loved learning, ranged through the classics and histories, and especially attended to ritual and etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: Rou from youth loved learning, ranged through the classics and histories, and especially attended to ritual and etiquette.

sentences.zh: 性強記，至於氏族內外，多所諳悉。

translations.literal: His nature was strongly retentive; regarding clans within and without, he was well acquainted with many.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was strongly retentive; regarding clans within and without, he was well acquainted with many.

sentences.zh: 初為世宗挽郎，出身司空行參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a mourning attendant for Gao Cheng; he entered office as acting staff member in the ministry of works.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a mourning attendant for Gao Cheng; he entered office as acting staff member in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 喪母，成喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he completed mourning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he completed mourning and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 永安中，除中堅將軍、奉車都尉，加冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was made steadfast general and chariot commandant, with added rank as champion general and palace gentleman for attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was made steadfast general and chariot commandant, with added rank as champion general and palace gentleman for attendance.

sentences.zh: 元象中，隨例到晉陽，高祖以為永安公府長流參軍，又令教授諸子。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he followed precedent to Jinyang; Gao Huan made him long-flowing staff member in Prince of Yong'an's establishment office and again ordered him to teach the princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he followed precedent to Jinyang; Gao Huan made him long-flowing staff member in Prince of Yong'an's establishment office and again ordered him to teach the princes.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除國子博士、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao he was made National University doctorate lecturer and palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was made National University doctorate lecturer and palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 魏收撰魏史，啟柔等與同其事。

translations.literal: Wei Shou compiled the History of Wei and memorialized that Rou and others should share in the task.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou compiled the History of Wei and memorialized that Rou and others should share in the task.

sentences.zh: 柔性頗專固，自是所聞，收常所嫌憚。

translations.literal: By nature Rou was rather gentle yet quite stubborn and self-willed—that was what people heard; Shou often resented and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Rou was pliant in disposition yet stubborn and set in his ways—that was the reputation he bore; Wei Shou often resented and feared him.

sentences.zh: 又參議律令。

translations.literal: He also took part in deliberating statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in deliberating statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 時議者以為立五等爵邑，承襲者無嫡子立嫡孫，無嫡孫立嫡子弟，無嫡子弟立嫡孫弟。

translations.literal: At the time deliberators held that in establishing the five ranks of enfeoffment and fiefs, when the inheritor had no direct son one established the direct grandson; when there was no direct grandson, the direct younger brother of the son; when there was no direct younger brother of the son, the direct younger brother of the grandson.
translations.idiomatic: At the time deliberators held that in establishing the five ranks of enfeoffment and fiefs, if the heir had no eldest son one named the eldest grandson; if no eldest grandson, the eldest son's younger brother; if none of those, the grandson's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 柔以為無嫡孫應立嫡曾孫，不應立嫡子弟。

translations.literal: Rou held that when there was no direct grandson one ought to establish the direct great-grandson, and one should not establish the direct younger brother of the son.
translations.idiomatic: Rou held that without an eldest grandson one ought to name the eldest great-grandson, and ought not name the eldest son's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 議曰：

translations.literal: The deliberation states:
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation reads:

sentences.zh: 柔案《禮》立適以長，故謂長子為嫡子。

translations.literal: Rou cites the Rites: establishing the heir by seniority is why the eldest son is called the direct son.
translations.idiomatic: Rou cites the Rites: the heir is established by seniority, which is why the eldest son is called the direct heir.

sentences.zh: 嫡子死，以嫡子之子為嫡孫，死則曾、玄亦然。

translations.literal: When the direct son dies, take the direct son's son as direct grandson; when he dies, great-grandson and great-great-grandson follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: When the direct heir dies, his son becomes the direct grandson; when that grandson dies, great-grandson and great-great-grandson follow in the same way.

sentences.zh: 然則嫡子之名，本為傳重。

translations.literal: Thus the name direct son exists fundamentally to transmit the main line.
translations.idiomatic: The title direct heir exists, then, to carry the main ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 故《喪服》曰：「庶子不為長子三年，不繼祖與禰也。

translations.literal: Hence the Mourning Dress says: A son by a concubine does not wear mourning three years for the eldest son—he does not continue grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Mourning Dress says, "A son by a concubine does not mourn the eldest son for three years—he does not continue grandfather and father."

sentences.zh: 《禮記》公儀仲子之喪：「檀弓曰：『何居，我未之前聞。

translations.literal: Record of Rites, the mourning for Gongyi Zhongzi: Zhan Gong said, What is this? I have never heard of it before.
translations.idiomatic: In the Record of Rites, on the mourning for Gongyi Zhongzi: Zhan Gong said, "What is this? I have never heard of it before."

sentences.zh: 仲子舍其孫而立其子何也？

translations.literal: Why did Zhongzi set aside his grandson and establish his son?
translations.idiomatic: "Why did Zhongzi set aside his grandson and name his son instead?"

sentences.zh: 』子服伯子曰：『仲子亦猶行古之道也，昔者文王舍伯邑考而立武王發，微子舍其孫盾而立弟衍，仲子亦猶行古之道也。

translations.literal: Zifu Bozi said: Zhongzi was also following the ancient way. In former times King Wen set aside Bo Yi Kao and established King Wu Fa; Weizi set aside his grandson Dun and established his younger brother Yan—Zhongzi too was following the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Zifu Bozi said, "Zhongzi was also following the ancient way. Long ago King Wen set aside Bo Yi Kao and established King Wu Fa; Weizi set aside his grandson Dun and established his younger brother Yan—Zhongzi too was following the ancient way."

sentences.zh: 』」鄭注曰：「伯子為親者諱耳，立子非也。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: Bozi was speaking euphemistically for a kinsman; establishing the son was not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says, "Bozi was speaking euphemistically for a kinsman; naming the son was not correct."

sentences.zh: 文王之立武王，權也。

translations.literal: King Wen's establishing King Wu was an expedient.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's establishing King Wu was an expedient.

sentences.zh: 微子嫡子死，立其弟衍，殷禮也。

translations.literal: When Weizi's direct son died he established his younger brother Yan—Yin rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Weizi's direct heir died he established his younger brother Yan—that was Yin rites.

sentences.zh: 」「子遊問諸孔子，孔子曰：『不，立孫。

translations.literal: Ziyou asked Confucius; Confucius said: No—establish the grandson.
translations.idiomatic: "Ziyou asked Confucius; Confucius said, 'No—establish the grandson.'"

sentences.zh: 』」注曰：「據《周禮》。

translations.literal: The commentary says: according to the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, "According to the Rites of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」然則商以嫡子死，立嫡子之母弟，周以嫡子死，立嫡子之子為嫡孫。

translations.literal: Thus in Shang, when the direct son died, they established the mother's younger brother of the direct son; in Zhou, when the direct son died, they established the direct son's son as direct grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in Shang, when the direct heir died, they named his mother's younger brother; in Zhou, when the direct heir died, they named his son as direct grandson.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋公羊》之義，嫡子有孫而死，質家親親先立弟，文家尊尊先立孫。

translations.literal: Thus the meaning of the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals: when the direct son has a grandson and dies, in the quality-oriented school kinship comes first and the younger brother is established; in the culture-oriented school honor comes first and the grandson is established.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Gongyang reading of the Spring and Autumn Annals: when the direct heir has a grandson and dies, the quality-oriented school, prizing kinship, establishes the younger brother first; the culture-oriented school, prizing rank, establishes the grandson first.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》云：「為父後者為出母無服。

translations.literal: The Mourning Dress says: One who becomes heir to the father wears no mourning for an expelled mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress says, "One who becomes heir to the father wears no mourning for an expelled mother."

sentences.zh: 」《小記》云：「祖父卒而後為祖母後者三年。

translations.literal: The Lesser Record says: When the grandfather dies, one who thereafter becomes heir to the grandmother wears mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Record says, "When the grandfather dies, one who thereafter becomes heir to the grandmother wears mourning three years."

sentences.zh: 」為出母無服者，喪者不祭故也。

translations.literal: The reason one who becomes heir to the father wears no mourning for an expelled mother is that the mourner does not sacrifice to her.
translations.idiomatic: He who becomes heir to the father wears no mourning for an expelled mother because the heir does not sacrifice to her.

sentences.zh: 為祖母三年者，大宗傳重故也。

translations.literal: The reason one wears three years for the grandmother is that the great lineage transmits the main line.
translations.idiomatic: He wears three years for the grandmother because the great lineage carries the main ancestral weight.

sentences.zh: 今議以嫡孫死而立嫡子母弟，嫡子母弟者則為父後矣。

translations.literal: Now the deliberation would, when the direct grandson dies, establish the mother's younger brother of the direct son; the mother's younger brother of the direct son would then become heir to the father.
translations.idiomatic: Now the deliberation would, when the direct grandson dies, name the direct son's mother's younger brother—who would then become heir to the father.

sentences.zh: 嫡子母弟本非承嫡，以無嫡，故得為父後。

translations.literal: The mother's younger brother of the direct son was originally not one who could inherit the direct line; only because there was no direct heir could he become heir to the father.
translations.idiomatic: That younger brother was never meant to inherit the direct line; only the absence of a direct heir would let him become heir to the father.

sentences.zh: 則嫡孫之弟，理亦應得為父後。

translations.literal: Then by principle the younger brother of the direct grandson should also be able to become heir to the father.
translations.idiomatic: By the same logic the direct grandson's younger brother ought to be able to become heir to the father.

sentences.zh: 則是父卒然後為祖後者服斬，旣得為祖服斬，而不得為傳重者，未之聞也。

translations.literal: Then one would wear the severest mourning for having become heir to the grandfather after the father's death; having obtained the right to mourn the grandfather with the severest grade, yet not being able to transmit the main line—I have never heard of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Then one would wear the severest mourning for becoming grandfather's heir only after the father's death—yet having earned that severest grade for the grandfather, one could not carry the main line. I have never heard of such a thing.

sentences.zh: 若用商家親親之義，本不應嫡子死而立嫡孫。

translations.literal: If one applied the Shang school's meaning of prizing kinship, one originally should not, when the direct son died, establish the direct grandson.
translations.idiomatic: If one followed the Shang school's kinship-first rule, one should not, when the direct heir died, establish the direct grandson at all.

sentences.zh: 若從周家尊尊之文，豈宜舍其孫而立其弟？

translations.literal: If one followed the Zhou school's culture of honoring rank, how could one set aside the grandson and establish the younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: If one followed the Zhou school's honor-first rule, how could one set aside the grandson and name the younger brother?

sentences.zh: 或文或質，愚用惑焉。

translations.literal: Whether culture or quality, I am perplexed in using them.
translations.idiomatic: Culture or quality—whichever one follows, I remain perplexed.

sentences.zh: 《小記》復云：「嫡婦不為舅姑後者，則姑姑為之小功。

translations.literal: The Lesser Record also says: When the direct daughter-in-law does not become heir to father-in-law and mother-in-law, then the father's sisters wear mourning in the lesser grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Record also says, "When the direct daughter-in-law does not become heir to her parents-in-law, the husband's sisters wear the lesser grade of mourning."

sentences.zh: 」注云：「謂夫有廢疾他故，若死無子不受重者。

translations.literal: The commentary says: meaning when the husband has crippling illness or other cause, or dies without a son who can receive the main line.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says this means when the husband has crippling illness or some other cause, or dies without a son who can receive the main line.

sentences.zh: 小功，庶婦之服。

translations.literal: Lesser grade is the dress of a concubine's wife.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser grade is the dress of a concubine's wife.

sentences.zh: 凡父母於子，舅姑於婦，將不傳重於嫡，及將所傳重者非嫡，服之皆如衆子庶婦也。

translations.literal: Whenever parents toward sons, or parents-in-law toward daughters-in-law, are about not to transmit the main line to the direct heir, or the one about to receive the transmitted main line is not the direct heir, the mourning worn is all like that for ordinary sons and concubines' wives.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever parents toward sons, or parents-in-law toward daughters-in-law, will not transmit the main line to the direct heir—or will transmit it to someone who is not the direct heir—the mourning worn is always that for ordinary sons and concubines' wives.

sentences.zh: 」言死無子者，謂絕世無子，非謂無嫡子。

translations.literal: Saying dies without a son means the line is cut off and there is no son—not that there is no direct son.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase dies without a son means the line is extinguished and there is no son at all—not that there is no direct heir.

sentences.zh: 如其有子，焉得云無後？

translations.literal: If he had a son, how could one say there was no heir?
translations.idiomatic: If he had a son, how could one say there was no heir?

sentences.zh: 夫雖廢疾無子，婦猶以嫡為名。

translations.literal: Though the husband had crippling illness and no son, the wife was still called direct by name.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the husband were crippled and sonless, the wife still bore the name of direct consort.

sentences.zh: 嫡名旣在，而欲廢其子者，其如禮何！

translations.literal: The name direct being present, yet wishing to set aside her son—how would that accord with ritual!
translations.idiomatic: With the title of direct consort still in place, yet wishing to set aside her son—how would that accord with ritual!

sentences.zh: 禮有損益，代相沿革，必謂宗嫡可得而變者，則為後服斬，亦宜有因而改。

translations.literal: Rites have increase and decrease, generation by generation revising along the way; if one must say the direct heir of the lineage can be changed, then the severest mourning for becoming heir ought also to be altered accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Rites wax and wane, revised from age to age; if one insists the lineage's direct heir can be changed at will, then the severest mourning for becoming heir ought to change accordingly as well.

sentences.zh: 七年夏卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, summer, he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died in summer, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 柔在史館未久，逢勒成之際，志存偏黨。

translations.literal: Rou had not long been in the historiography bureau when he met the completion of the enterprise; his intent harbored partisan bias.
translations.idiomatic: Rou had not long served in the historiography bureau when the great compilation was finished; his intent harbored partisan bias.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》中與其內外通親者並虛美過實，深為時論所譏焉。

translations.literal: In the Book of Wei, those with whom he had close kinship inside and outside were all embellished beyond fact; he was deeply ridiculed in the talk of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Wei, kinsmen within and outside his circle were all painted brighter than truth; the age ridiculed him sharply for it.

sentences.zh: 馮偉，字偉節，中山安喜人也。

translations.literal: Feng Wei, styled Weijie, was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Wei, styled Weijie, came from Anxi in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，衣冠甚偉，見者肅然敬憚。

translations.literal: His height was eight chi; cap and robes were very imposing; those who saw him were solemn and held him in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall; cap and robes cut an imposing figure, and those who met him felt a solemn awe.

sentences.zh: 少從李寶鼎遊學，李重其聰敏，恒別意試問之，多所通解，尤明《禮傳》。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Li Baoding in study; Li valued his quick wit and constantly set him special questions to test him; he understood many things and was especially clear in the Ritual tradition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Li Baoding. Li prized his quick wit and constantly set him special tests; he answered most of them, and was especially clear in the Ritual tradition.

sentences.zh: 後還鄉里，閉門不出將三十年，不問生產，不交賓客，專精覃思，無所不通。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district, shut his door and did not go out for nearly thirty years, not asking after livelihood, not receiving guests, concentrating his thought alone—there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned home, shut his door, and for nearly thirty years did not go out—caring nothing for livelihood, receiving no guests, bending all his thought to learning until nothing lay beyond him.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王出鎮定州，以禮迎接，命書三至，縣令親至其門，猶辭疾不起。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao commandery went out to garrison Dingzhou and received him with ritual; orders in writing came three times, and the magistrate came in person to his gate—yet he still pleaded illness and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao commandery went out to garrison Dingzhou he received Wei with full ritual courtesy; written summons came three times and the magistrate came to his gate in person—yet Wei still pleaded illness and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 王將命駕致請，佐史前後星馳報之，縣令又自為其整冠履，不得已而出。

translations.literal: The prince was about to drive in person to invite him; aides before and behind galloped in relays to report; the magistrate again himself set his cap and shoes in order for him; he had no choice but to go out.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was about to drive out himself to invite him; aides galloped back and forth with reports; the magistrate again arranged cap and shoes for him at the door; at last he had no choice but to go out.

sentences.zh: 王下廳事迎之，止其拜伏，分階而上，留之賓館，甚見禮重。

translations.literal: The prince came down from the hall affairs to welcome him, stopped his prostrations, shared the steps going up, lodged him in the guest hostel, and showed him great ritual esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The prince came down from the hall to welcome him, stopped his prostrations, shared the steps as they went up, lodged him in the guest quarters, and honored him with great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 王將舉充秀才，固辭不就。

translations.literal: The prince was about to recommend him as a flourishing talent; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The prince meant to recommend him as a flourishing talent; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 歲餘請還。

translations.literal: After more than a year he asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 王知其不願拘束，以禮發遣，贈遺甚厚，一無所納，唯受時服而已。

translations.literal: The prince knew he did not wish to be constrained; he sent him off with ritual and gave rich gifts; he accepted nothing except the seasonal garments of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The prince knew he would not be bound; he sent him off with ritual and rich gifts. Wei accepted nothing but the seasonal garments offered at parting.

sentences.zh: 及還，終不交人事，郡守縣令每親至其門。

translations.literal: On returning he still would not mix in human affairs; the commandery administrator and magistrate each came in person to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once home he still would not mix in worldly affairs; commandery administrators and magistrates came in person to his gate.

sentences.zh: 歲時或置羊酒，亦辭不納。

translations.literal: At the seasons they sometimes set out sheep and wine; he also declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the seasons they sometimes sent sheep and wine; he declined those as well.

sentences.zh: 門徒束脩，一毫不受。

translations.literal: From disciples, dried meat for the teacher—he did not accept a single strand.
translations.idiomatic: From disciples, the dried meat of tuition—not a single strand would he take.

sentences.zh: 耕而飯，蠶而衣，簞食瓢飲，不改其樂，竟以壽終。

translations.literal: He plowed for food and raised silkworms for clothing, bamboo basket for rice and gourd dipper for drink, not changing his joy, and in the end died at full years.
translations.idiomatic: He plowed for food and raised silkworms for clothing, ate from a bamboo basket and drank from a gourd dipper, and did not change his joy; in the end he died at full years.

sentences.zh: 張買奴，平原人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Mainu was a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mainu came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 經義該博，門徒千餘人。

translations.literal: His mastery of the classics was comprehensive and broad; his disciples numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His command of the classics was comprehensive; his disciples numbered more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 諸儒咸推重之，名聲甚盛。

translations.literal: The Confucians all pushed him forward in esteem; his fame and voice were very great.
translations.idiomatic: The Confucians all pushed him forward in esteem, and his fame was very great.

sentences.zh: 歷太學博士、國子助教，天保中卒。

translations.literal: He passed through erudite of the Imperial University and assistant teacher of the National University, and died in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: He served as erudite of the Imperial University and assistant teacher of the National University, and died in the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 劉軌思，渤海人也。

translations.literal: Liu Guisi was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guisi came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 說《詩》甚精。

translations.literal: His exposition of the Odes was very refined.
translations.idiomatic: His exposition of the Odes was very refined.

sentences.zh: 少事同郡劉敬和，敬和事同郡程歸則，故其鄉曲多為《詩》者。

translations.literal: In youth he served Liu Jinghe of the same commandery; Jinghe served Cheng Guize of the same commandery—thus in their home district many became students of the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Liu Jinghe of the same commandery; Jinghe had studied under Cheng Guize of the same commandery—thus in their home district many became students of the Odes.

sentences.zh: 軌思，天統中任國子博士。

translations.literal: Guisi in the Tiantong era served as erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiantong era Guisi served as erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 鮑季詳，渤海人也。

translations.literal: Bao Jixiang was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jixiang came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 甚明《禮》，聽其離文析句，自然大略可解。

translations.literal: He was very clear in the Rites; hearing him separate text and parse clauses, one naturally grasped the general meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He was very clear in the Rites; hearing him separate text and parse clauses, one naturally grasped the general meaning.

sentences.zh: 兼通《左氏春秋》，少時恒為李寶鼎都講，後亦自有徒衆，諸儒稱之。

translations.literal: He was also versed in the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals; in youth he was constantly chief lecturer for Li Baoding, and later also had his own following; the Confucians praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also versed in the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals. In youth he had long served as chief lecturer for Li Baoding; later he gathered his own following, and the Confucians praised him.

sentences.zh: 天統中，卒於太學博士。

translations.literal: In the Tiantong era he died as erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiantong era he died while serving as erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 從弟長暄，兼通《禮傳》。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Changxuan was also versed in the Ritual tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Changxuan was also versed in the Ritual tradition.

sentences.zh: 武平末，為任城王湝丞相掾，恒在京教授貴遊子弟。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was staff aide to Chancellor Prince of Rencheng Tao, and constantly taught in the capital the sons of noble houses.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was staff aide to Chancellor Prince of Rencheng Tao and constantly taught in the capital the sons of noble houses.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後，歸鄉里講經，卒於家。

translations.literal: After Qi perished he returned to his home district to lecture on the classics and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell he returned home to lecture on the classics and died there.

sentences.zh: 邢峙，字士峻，河間鄚人也，少好學，耽玩墳典，遊學燕、趙之間，通《二禮》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Xing Zhi, styled Shijun, was a man of Mo in Hejian; from youth he loved learning, immersed himself in the canonical tomes, and traveled in study between Yan and Zhao, mastering the two Rites and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zhi, styled Shijun, came from Mo in Hejian. From youth he loved learning, immersed himself in the canonical tomes, and traveled between Yan and Zhao until he mastered the two Rites and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 天保初，郡舉孝廉，授四門博士，遷國子助教，以經入授皇太子。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao the commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he was appointed erudite of the Four Gates, promoted to assistant teacher of the National University, and entered the palace to instruct the heir apparent in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao the commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he was appointed erudite of the Four Gates, promoted to assistant teacher of the National University, and entered the palace to instruct the heir apparent in the classics.

sentences.zh: 峙方正純厚，有儒者之風。

translations.literal: Zhi was square, upright, pure, and thick, with the bearing of a Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was square, upright, pure, and steadfast, with the bearing of a true Confucian.

sentences.zh: 廚宰進太子食，有菜曰「」邪蒿」，峙命去之，曰：「此菜有不正之名，非殿下所宜食。

translations.literal: The kitchen steward presented the heir apparent's food; there was a dish called xiehao; Zhi ordered it removed and said: This dish has an inauspicious name; it is not what Your Highness should eat.
translations.idiomatic: When the kitchen steward presented the heir apparent's meal, one dish was a herb called xiehao. Zhi ordered it removed and said, "This plant bears an inauspicious name—it is not food fit for Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」顯祖聞而嘉之，賜以被褥縑纊，拜國子博士。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu heard and praised this, bestowing quilts and silks, and appointing him erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu heard of it and praised him, bestowing quilts and silks and appointing him erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，除清河太守，有惠政，民吏愛之。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangjian he was made administrator of Qinghe; his administration had benevolent policies and officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huangjian he was made administrator of Qinghe; his rule was benevolent, and officials and people loved him.

sentences.zh: 以年老謝病歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Because of age he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When age weighed on him he resigned on grounds of illness, returned home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 劉晝，字孔昭，渤海阜城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhou, styled Kongzhao, was a man of Fucheng in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhou, styled Kongzhao, came from Fucheng in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，愛學，負笈從師，伏膺無倦。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he loved learning, carried a book box and followed teachers, bending his breast without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he loved learning, carried his book box from teacher to teacher, and bent to his studies without weariness.

sentences.zh: 與儒者李寶鼎同鄉里，甚相親愛，受其《三禮》。

translations.literal: With the Confucian Li Baoding he was of the same home district and very close in affection; he received from him the three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: With the Confucian Li Baoding he shared a home district and deep affection; from Li he received the three Rites.

sentences.zh: 又就馬敬德習《服氏春秋》，俱通大義。

translations.literal: He also went to Ma Jingde to study the Fu clan Spring and Autumn Annals; both mastered the great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied the Fu clan Spring and Autumn Annals under Ma Jingde; both mastered the great meaning.

sentences.zh: 恨下里少墳籍，便杖策入都。

translations.literal: He regretted that in his home district there were few canonical tomes and, staff in hand, entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He regretted that his home district held few canonical tomes and, staff in hand, made for the capital.

sentences.zh: 知太府少卿宋世良家多書，乃造焉。

translations.literal: Knowing that Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse Song Shiliang's household had many books, he went to him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse Song Shiliang's household held many books, he went to him.

sentences.zh: 世良納之。

translations.literal: Shiliang took him in.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang took him in.

sentences.zh: 恣意披覽，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: He read at will day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: He read at will, day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 河清初，還冀州，舉季才入京，考策不第。

translations.literal: At the start of Heqingchu he returned to Jizhou; recommended as a seasonal talent he entered the capital; in the examination composition he did not place.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Heqingchu he returned to Jizhou; recommended as a seasonal talent he entered the capital, but failed the examination composition.

sentences.zh: 乃恨不學屬文，方復緝綴辭藻，言甚古拙。

translations.literal: He then resented not having studied composition, and only then began to weave literary ornament—his language was very archaic and clumsy.
translations.idiomatic: He then resented not having studied composition and only then began to weave literary ornament—his language was very archaic and clumsy.

sentences.zh: 制一首賦以「六合」為名，自謂絕倫，吟諷不輟。

translations.literal: He composed one fu taking Six Harmonies as its title, calling it peerless, and chanted it without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a fu titled Six Harmonies, called it peerless, and chanted it without cease.

sentences.zh: 乃嘆曰：「儒者勞而少工，見於斯矣。

translations.literal: He sighed and said: The Confucian toils yet achieves little—here it is seen.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "The Confucian toils yet achieves little—here it is seen."

sentences.zh: 我讀儒書二十餘年而答策不第，始學作文，便得如是。

translations.literal: I read Confucian books more than twenty years yet failed the examination composition; I began to study writing and at once could do this.
translations.idiomatic: "I read Confucian books for more than twenty years yet failed the examination; I began to study writing and at once could do this."

sentences.zh: 」曾以此賦呈魏收，收謂人曰：「賦名六合，其愚已甚，及見其賦，又愚於名。」

translations.literal: He once presented this fu to Wei Shou; Shou told others: The fu is named Six Harmonies—its folly is already great; when I saw the fu, it was more foolish than the name.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented this fu to Wei Shou. Shou told others, "The fu is named Six Harmonies—its folly is already great; when I saw the fu, it was more foolish than the name."

sentences.zh: 晝又撰《高才不遇傳》三篇。

translations.literal: Zhou also composed three pieces of the Biography of Great Talent Unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou also composed three pieces of the Biography of Great Talent Unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 在皇建、大寧之朝，又頻上書，言亦切直，多非世要，終不見收采。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian and Daning reigns he again repeatedly submitted memorials; his words were also blunt and direct, mostly not what the age required, and in the end he was never accepted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangjian and Daning reigns he again and again submitted memorials—blunt and direct, mostly unwelcome to the age—and in the end was never employed.

sentences.zh: 自謂博物奇才，言好矜大，每云：「使我數十卷書行於後世，不易齊景之千駟也。

translations.literal: He considered himself broadly learned and a rare talent, spoke fondly in grand terms, and often said: Let a few dozen volumes of mine circulate in later ages—it is no harder than Duke Jing of Qi's thousand four-horse teams.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself broadly learned and a rare talent, spoke in fond grand terms, and often said, "Let a few dozen volumes of mine circulate in later ages—it is no harder than Duke Jing of Qi's thousand four-horse teams."

sentences.zh: 」而容止舒緩，舉動不倫，由是竟無仕進。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing was easy and slow, his movements not of the proper kind—because of this in the end he had no advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his bearing was easy and slow and his movements ill-suited to propriety—because of this he never advanced in office.

sentences.zh: 天統中，卒於家，年五十二。

translations.literal: In the Tiantong era he died at home, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiantong era he died at home, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 馬敬德，河間人也。

translations.literal: Ma Jingde was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jingde came from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少好儒術，負笈隨大儒徐遵明學《詩》、《禮》，略通大義而不能精。

translations.literal: In youth he loved Confucian studies, carried a book box and followed the great Confucian Xu Zunming in studying the Odes and Rites, grasping the great meaning but unable to refine it.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved Confucian studies, carried his book box, and followed the great Confucian Xu Zunming in the Odes and Rites—grasping the great meaning but unable to refine it.

sentences.zh: 遂留意於《春秋左氏》，沉思研求，晝夜不倦，解義為諸儒所稱。

translations.literal: He then turned his mind to the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, pondering and seeking deeply day and night without weariness; his explication of meaning was praised by the Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned his mind to the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, pondering it day and night without weariness; his explication of meaning won praise from the Confucians.

sentences.zh: 教授於燕、趙間，生徒隨之者衆。

translations.literal: He lectured between Yan and Zhao; the disciples who followed him were many.
translations.idiomatic: He taught between Yan and Zhao, and the disciples who trailed after him were a great crowd.

sentences.zh: 河間郡王每於教學追之，將舉為孝廉，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Whenever he gave instruction the Prince of Hejian Commandery would pursue him; [the prince] meant to recommend him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he taught, the Prince of Hejian Commandery would press close upon him and meant to put him forward as Filial and Incorrupt; Jingde refused outright and would not take the post.

sentences.zh: 乃詣州求舉秀才。

translations.literal: So he went to the province to seek nomination as Emeritus Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: So he went to the province and asked to be nominated as Emeritus Scholar.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才例取文士，州將以其純儒，無意推薦。

translations.literal: By rule Emeritus Scholar nominations took literary men; the provincial commander, seeing he was a pure Confucian, had no wish to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Emeritus Scholar nominations were supposed to go to men of letters; the provincial commander, seeing a pure Confucian before him, had no mind to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 敬德請試方略，乃策問之，所答五條，皆有文理。

translations.literal: Jingde requested a trial on strategy and tactics, so [the commander] questioned him in that vein; of the five answers he gave, each had literary sense.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde asked to be tested on strategy and tactics instead. The commander put policy questions to him; all five of his answers were literate and sound.

sentences.zh: 乃欣然舉送至京。

translations.literal: [The commander] then gladly sent him on to the capital with recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The commander was pleased and sent him on to the capital with his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 依秀才策問，唯得中第，乃請試經業，問十條並通。

translations.literal: Per the Emeritus Scholar policy questions, he only achieved middling rank; then he requested examination in classical studies—of ten questions he answered all correctly.
translations.idiomatic: On the Emeritus Scholar policy examination he only reached middling rank; then he asked to be tested in the classics and answered all ten questions correctly.

sentences.zh: 擢授國子助教，遷太學博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Adjunct of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, then transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to adjunct of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, then transferred to erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 天統初，除國子博士。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiantong he was made Erudite of the Directorate of the Sons of the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he was made erudite of the Directorate of the Sons of the State.

sentences.zh: 世祖為後主擇師傅，趙彥深進之，入為侍講。

translations.literal: When Shizu chose tutors for the Later Lord, Zhao Yanshen recommended him; he entered [court] as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was choosing tutors for the Later Lord, Zhao Yanshen put him forward and he entered court as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 其妻夢猛獸將來向之，敬德走超叢棘，妻伏地不敢動。

translations.literal: His wife dreamed a fierce beast was coming toward her; Jingde ran and leaped through a bramble thicket, while his wife lay flat on the ground and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: His wife dreamed a fierce beast was bearing down on her. Jingde ran and vaulted through a bramble thicket; his wife lay flat on the ground and did not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 敬德占之曰：「吾當得大官。

translations.literal: Jingde divined and said: "I am about to receive high office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde read the dream and said, "I am about to receive high office.

sentences.zh: 超棘，過九卿也。

translations.literal: Leaping the thicket surpasses the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Vaulting the thicket means passing the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 爾伏地，夫人也。

translations.literal: You lying flat—that is the wife of a grandee."
translations.idiomatic: You lying flat—that is the wife of a grandee."

sentences.zh: 」後主旣不好學，敬德侍講甚疏，時時以《春秋》入授。

translations.literal: The Later Lord by then cared little for study; Jingde's lecturing was very sparse, but from time to time he would enter and teach the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Later Lord cared little for learning; Jingde's lectures grew thin, though now and then he would come in and teach the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 武平初，猶以師傅之恩，超拜國子祭酒，加儀同三司、金紫光祿大夫，領瀛州大中正，卒。

translations.literal: At the start of Wuping, still in gratitude for tutor's favor, he was advanced to Director of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, given additional rank as Full Powers Equal to the Three Dukes and Grand Master with Golden Cap and Purple Tassel, made Grand Rectifier of Ying Province, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuping, still out of gratitude for his service as tutor, he was advanced to director of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, given full powers equal to the three dukes and the golden-cap grand master rank, made grand rectifier of Ying Province, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈開府、瀛滄安州諸軍事、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Commander Who Opens a Government Office and Governor of Ying, Cang, and An provinces in military affairs over Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the rank of commander who opens a government office and governor of Ying, Cang, and An provinces in military affairs over Ying.

sentences.zh: 其後侍書張景仁封王。

translations.literal: Afterward the attendant calligrapher Zhang Jingren was enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the attendant calligrapher Zhang Jingren was enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 趙彥深云：「何容侍書封王，侍講翻無封爵。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshen said: "How can an attendant calligrapher be made prince while the lecturer-in-attendance has no enfeoffment or rank?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen said, "How can an attendant calligrapher be made a prince while the lecturer-in-attendance has no title at all?"

sentences.zh: 」於是亦封敬德廣漢郡王。

translations.literal: So Jingde too was enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: So Jingde too was enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子元熙襲。

translations.literal: His son Yuanxi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanxi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 元熙字長明，少傳父業，兼事文藻。

translations.literal: Yuanxi, styled Changming, in youth transmitted his father's learning and also cultivated literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi, styled Changming, in youth took up his father's learning and also cultivated literary polish.

sentences.zh: 以父故，自青州集曹參軍超遷通直侍郎，待詔文林館，轉正員。

translations.literal: Because of his father he was advanced from collection-office staff officer in Qing Province to attendant gentleman through direct access, awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall, and was made a regular appointee.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father he was vaulted from collection-office staff officer in Qing Province to attendant gentleman through direct access, awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall, and was made a regular appointee.

sentences.zh: 武平中，皇太子將講《孝經》，有司請擇師友，帝曰：「馬元熙朕師之子，文學不惡，可令教兒。

translations.literal: In Wuping the heir apparent was about to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; the authorities asked to choose tutors and companions. The emperor said: "Ma Yuanxi is my tutor's son; his letters are not bad—let him teach the boy."
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping the heir apparent was to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and the authorities asked who should teach him. The emperor said, "Ma Yuanxi is my tutor's son; his letters are not bad—let him teach the boy."

sentences.zh: 」於是以《孝經》入授皇太子，儒者榮其世載。

translations.literal: So he entered to teach the Classic of Filial Piety to the heir apparent, and Confucians gloried that the office ran in the family.
translations.idiomatic: So he came in to teach the Classic of Filial Piety to the heir apparent, and the Confucians took pride that the post had stayed in one line.

sentences.zh: 性和厚，在內甚得名譽，皇太子亦親敬之。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and generous; within the palace he won great repute, and the heir apparent too treated him with personal respect.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was mild and generous; within the palace he won great repute, and the heir apparent treated him with personal respect.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒於秦王文學。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as literary aide to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's Kaihuang era he died as literary aide to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 張景仁者，濟北人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingren was a man of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingren was a man of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 幼孤家貧，以學書為業，遂工草隸，選補內書生。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he took up the study of writing as his craft, and came to excel at cursive and clerical script; he was selected and made up as an inner calligraphy student.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he took up writing as his trade and came to excel at cursive and clerical script; he was selected and made up as an inner calligraphy student.

sentences.zh: 與魏郡姚元標、潁川韓毅、同郡袁買奴、滎陽李超等齊名，世宗並引為賓客。

translations.literal: With Yao Yuanbiao of Wei Commandery, Han Yi of Yingchuan, Yuan Mainu of the same commandery, and Li Chao of Xingyang he was famed alike; Shizong brought them all in as guests.
