translations.idiomatic: With Yao Yuanbiao of Wei Commandery, Han Yi of Yingchuan, Yuan Mainu of the same commandery, and Li Chao of Xingyang he stood among the famous; Shizong brought them all in as guests.

sentences.zh: 天保八年，勑授太原王紹德書，除開府參軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao an edict appointed him to write for Prince of Taiyuan Shaode and made him staff officer who opens a government office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao's eighth year an edict appointed him to write for Prince of Taiyuan Shaode and made him staff officer who opens a government office.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，世祖選善書人性行淳謹者令侍書，景仁遂被引擢。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace, Shizu chose men skilled at writing whose conduct was pure and cautious to serve as attendant calligraphers; Jingren was then brought forward and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord was still in the Eastern Palace, Shizu chose men skilled at writing whose conduct was pure and cautious to serve as attendant calligraphers, and Jingren was brought forward and promoted.

sentences.zh: 小心恭慎，後主愛之，呼為博士。

translations.literal: Careful and reverent, he was loved by the Later Lord, who called him "Doctor."
translations.idiomatic: Careful and reverent, he won the Later Lord's favor; the lord called him "Doctor."

sentences.zh: 歷太子門大夫、員外散騎常侍、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He passed through gate master of the heir apparent, supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office, and grand advisor for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through gate master of the heir apparent, supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office, and grand advisor for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 後主登祚，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord took the throne he was made attendant at the scribal office through direct access.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne he was made attendant at the scribal office through direct access.

sentences.zh: 及奏，禦筆點除「通」字，遂正常侍。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the imperial brush struck through the character "through" and he became regular attendant at the scribal office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the imperial brush struck through the word "through," and he became regular attendant at the scribal office.

sentences.zh: 左右與語，猶稱博士。

translations.literal: Those close to him in speech still called him Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Those close to him still called him Doctor in conversation.

sentences.zh: 胡人何洪珍有寵於後主，欲得通婚朝士，以景仁在內官位稍高，遂為其兄子取景仁第二息子瑜之女。

translations.literal: The barbarian Hong Zhen had the Later Lord's favor and wished to marry his clan to court gentlemen; because Jingren's inner-court post was somewhat high, [Hong Zhen] took Jingren's second son Ziyu's daughter for his elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian Hong Zhen had the Later Lord's favor and wished to marry his kin into the court; because Jingren's inner-court post was somewhat high, he took Jingren's second son Ziyu's daughter for his elder brother's son.

sentences.zh: 因此表裏，恩遇日隆。

translations.literal: Through this inside-out tie, favor and grace grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Through that inside-out tie, favor and grace grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 景仁多疾，每遣徐之範等治療，給藥物珍羞，中使問疾，相望於道。

translations.literal: Jingren was often ill; each time [the court] sent Xu Zhifan and others to treat him, giving medicines and delicacies; palace envoys inquired after his illness one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren was often ill; each time the court sent Xu Zhifan and others to treat him with medicines and delicacies, while palace envoys asking after his health filed along the road.

sentences.zh: 是後，勑有司恒就宅送御食。

translations.literal: After that, an edict ordered the authorities always to send imperial food to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: After that an edict ordered the authorities always to send imperial food to his house.

sentences.zh: 遷假儀同三司，銀青光祿大夫，食恒山縣幹。

translations.literal: He was moved to acting full powers equal to the three dukes and grand master with silver cap and bluegreen tassel, drawing dry rations from Hengshan county.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to acting full powers equal to the three dukes and grand master with silver cap and bluegreen tassel, drawing dry rations from Hengshan county.

sentences.zh: 車駕或有行幸，在道宿處，每送步障為遮風寒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went out on progress, at each night's lodging along the way they would send portable screens to keep off wind and cold.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went out on progress, at each night's lodging along the way they sent portable screens to keep off wind and cold.

sentences.zh: 進位儀同三司、尋加開府，侍書、餘官並如故。

translations.literal: He advanced to full powers equal to the three dukes; soon he was further given commander who opens a government office, while attendant calligrapher and his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to full powers equal to the three dukes; soon he was further given commander who opens a government office, while his post as attendant calligrapher and his other offices stayed as they were.

sentences.zh: 每旦須參，卽在東宮停止。

translations.literal: Each morning he had to attend court and would lodge in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he had to attend court and lodged in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 及立文林館，中人鄧長颙希旨，奏令總制館事，除侍中。

translations.literal: When the Wenlin Hall was established, the inner attendant Deng Changyu, to please [the ruler], memorialized that [Jingren] should oversee the hall's affairs; he was made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenlin Hall was established, the inner attendant Deng Changyu, to please the ruler, memorialized that Jingren should oversee the hall; he was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 四年，封建安王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 洪珍死後，長顒猶存舊款，更相彌縫，得無墜退。

translations.literal: After Hong Zhen died, Changyu still kept the old bond and they continued to smooth things over for each other, so he did not fall back.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong Zhen died, Changyu still kept the old bond; they continued to smooth things over for each other, and Jingren did not fall back.

sentences.zh: 除中書監，以疾卒。

translations.literal: He was made director of the masters of writing and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the masters of writing and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、齊濟等五州刺史、司空公。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given palace attendant, governor of the five provinces Qi, Ji, and others, and minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given palace attendant, governor of the five provinces Qi, Ji, and others, and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 景仁出自寒微，本無識見，一旦開府、侍中、封王。

translations.literal: Jingren came from humble beginnings and originally had no discernment; in a single stroke he became commander who opens a government office, palace attendant, and prince.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren came from humble beginnings and originally had no discernment; in a single stroke he became commander who opens a government office, palace attendant, and prince.

sentences.zh: 其妻姓奇，莫知氏族所出，容制音辭，事事庸俚。

translations.literal: His wife's surname was Qi; no one knew what clan she came from. Her bearing, voice, and speech were vulgar in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's surname was Qi; no one knew what clan she came from. Her bearing, voice, and speech were vulgar in every respect.

sentences.zh: 旣詔除王妃，與諸公主、郡君同在朝謁之例，見者為其慚悚。

translations.literal: Once she was enfeoffed by edict as princess consort and stood in the same court-audience order as the princesses and commandery ladies, those who saw her felt shame and alarm for her.
translations.idiomatic: Once she was enfeoffed by edict as princess consort and stood in court-audience with the princesses and commandery ladies; those who saw her felt shame and alarm on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 子瑜薄傳父業，更無餘伎，以洪珍故，擢授中書舍人，轉給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Ziyu thinly transmitted his father's craft and had no other skill; because of Hong Zhen he was advanced to drafting officer of the masters of writing, then moved to attendant gentleman at the yellow gate who serves matters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyu thinly transmitted his father's craft and had no other skill; because of Hong Zhen he was advanced to drafting officer of the masters of writing, then moved to attendant gentleman at the yellow gate who serves matters.

sentences.zh: 長息子玉，起家員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ziyu began his career as supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ziyu began his career as supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office.

sentences.zh: 景仁性本卑謙，及用胡人巷伯之勢，坐致通顯，誌操頗改，漸成驕傲。

translations.literal: Jingren's nature was originally humble, but once he used the power of the barbarian eunuch chamberlain he rose to conspicuous eminence; his resolve changed somewhat and he gradually grew proud.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren's nature was originally humble, but once he rode the barbarian eunuch chamberlain's power to conspicuous eminence his resolve shifted and he gradually grew proud.

sentences.zh: 良馬輕裘，徒從擁冗，高門廣宇，當衢向街。

translations.literal: Fine horses and light furs, attendants in a throng, high gates and broad halls facing the crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Fine horses and light furs, attendants in a throng, high gates and broad halls facing the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 諸子不思其本，自許貴遊。

translations.literal: His sons did not reflect on their origins and styled themselves noble wanderers.
translations.idiomatic: His sons did not reflect on their origins and styled themselves noble wanderers.

sentences.zh: 自蒼頡以來，八體取進，一人而已。

translations.literal: Since Cang Jie, of those who advanced through the eight script styles, he alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since Cang Jie, of those who advanced through the eight script styles, he alone.

sentences.zh: 權會，字正理，河間鄚人也。

translations.literal: Quan Hui, styled Zhengli, was a man of Mo in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Hui, styled Zhengli, was a man of Mo in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 誌尚沈雅，動遵禮則。

translations.literal: His aims were deep and refined; in movement he followed ritual rule.
translations.idiomatic: His aims were deep and refined; in movement he followed ritual rule.

sentences.zh: 少受《鄭易》，探賾索隱，妙盡幽微，《詩》、《書》、《三禮》，文義該洽，兼明風角，妙識玄象。

translations.literal: In youth he received Zheng's Changes, probing the hidden and seeking the obscure until he had exhausted the subtle; in the Odes, Documents, and Three Rites his literary meaning was comprehensive; he was also clear in wind and horn divination and had fine insight into dark signs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied Zheng's Changes, probing the hidden until he had exhausted the subtle; in the Odes, Documents, and Three Rites his literary meaning was comprehensive; he was also clear in wind and horn divination and had fine insight into dark signs.

sentences.zh: 魏武定初，本郡貢孝廉，策居上第，解褐四門博士。

translations.literal: At the start of Wei Wuding his native commandery presented him as Filial and Incorrupt; in policy examination he ranked at the top and doffed the headcloth as erudite of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wei Wuding his native commandery presented him as Filial and Incorrupt; in policy examination he ranked at the top and doffed the headcloth as erudite of the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 樸射崔暹引為館客，甚敬重焉，命世子達拏盡師傅之禮，會因此聞達。

translations.literal: Supervisor Cui Xian brought him in as hall guest and greatly respected him, ordering the heir Da to perform all a tutor's rites toward him; Hui thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Cui Xian brought him in as hall guest and greatly respected him, ordering the heir Da to perform all a tutor's rites toward him; Hui thereby became known.

sentences.zh: 暹欲薦會與馬敬德等為諸王師，會性恬靜，不慕榮勢，恥於左宦，固辭。

translations.literal: Xian wished to recommend Hui together with Ma Jingde and others as tutors to the princes; Hui's nature was tranquil and he did not covet glory or power, ashamed of left-hand office—he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xian wished to recommend Hui together with Ma Jingde and others as tutors to the princes; Hui's nature was tranquil and he did not covet glory or power, ashamed of left-hand office, and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 暹亦識其意，遂罷薦舉。

translations.literal: Xian also understood his intent and so stopped the recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also understood his intent and stopped the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 尋被尚書符追著作，修國史，監知太史局事。

translations.literal: Soon he was pursued by an order from the masters of writing to serve as author, revise the national history, and oversee affairs of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was pursued by an order from the masters of writing to serve as author, revise the national history, and oversee affairs of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，轉加中散大夫，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In Huangjian he was further made grand master of the scattered cohort; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangjian he was further made grand master of the scattered cohort; the rest remained as before.

sentences.zh: 會參掌雖繁，教授不闕。

translations.literal: Though his concurrent duties were many, he did not neglect teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Though his concurrent duties were many, he did not neglect teaching.

sentences.zh: 性甚儒懦，似不能言，及臨機答難，酬報如響。

translations.literal: His nature was very Confucian and timid, as if he could not speak; yet when facing a challenge on the spot his replies came like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was very Confucian and timid, as if he could not speak; yet when facing a challenge on the spot his replies came like an echo.

sentences.zh: 動必稽古，辭不虛發，由是為儒宗所推。

translations.literal: In movement he always checked against antiquity; his words were never empty—therefore the Confucian leaders pushed him forward.
translations.idiomatic: In movement he always checked against antiquity; his words were never empty, and the Confucian leaders pushed him forward.

sentences.zh: 而貴遊子弟慕其德義者，或就其宅，或寄宿鄰家，晝夜承間，受其學業。

translations.literal: Yet noble wanderers' sons who admired his virtue and righteousness would come to his house or lodge with neighbors nearby, day and night seizing intervals to receive his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sons of noble wanderers who admired his virtue and righteousness would come to his house or lodge with neighbors nearby, day and night seizing intervals to receive his learning.

sentences.zh: 會欣然演說，未嘗懈怠。

translations.literal: Hui would lecture gladly and never slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Hui would lecture gladly and never slacken.

sentences.zh: 雖明風角，解玄象，至於私室，輒不及言，學徒有請問者，終無所說。

translations.literal: Though he was clear in wind and horn and understood dark signs, in private quarters he never spoke of them; when students asked, in the end he said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was clear in wind and horn and understood dark signs, in private quarters he never spoke of them; when students asked, in the end he said nothing.

sentences.zh: 每云：「此學可知不可言。

translations.literal: He would always say: "This learning can be known but cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: He would always say, "This learning can be known but cannot be spoken.

sentences.zh: 諸君並貴遊子弟，不由此進，何煩問也。

translations.literal: You are all sons of noble wanderers; you do not advance by this path—why trouble to ask?"
translations.idiomatic: You are all sons of noble wanderers; you do not advance by this path—why trouble to ask?"

sentences.zh: 」會唯有一子，亦不以此術教之，其謹密也如此。

translations.literal: Hui had only one son and did not teach him this art either; such was his caution and secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had only one son and did not teach him this art either; such was his caution and secrecy.

sentences.zh: 曾令家人遠行，久而不反。

translations.literal: Once he sent a household member on a distant journey who was long in returning.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent a household member on a distant journey who was long in returning.

sentences.zh: 其行人還，垂欲至宅，乃逢寒雪，寄息他舍。

translations.literal: When the traveler came back, just about to reach the house, he met with cold snow and lodged at another inn.
translations.idiomatic: When the traveler came back, just about to reach the house, he met with cold snow and lodged at another inn.

sentences.zh: 會方處學堂講說，忽有旋風瞥然，吹雪入戶。

translations.literal: Hui was in the lecture hall giving instruction when suddenly a whirlwind flashed by and blew snow into the room.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was in the lecture hall giving instruction when suddenly a whirlwind flashed by and blew snow into the room.

sentences.zh: 會乃笑曰：「行人至，何意中停。

translations.literal: Hui then laughed and said: "The traveler has arrived—why stop midway?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui then laughed and said, "The traveler has arrived—why stop midway?"

sentences.zh: 」遂命使人令詣某處追尋，果如其語。

translations.literal: He then ordered a man sent to seek him at a certain place; it turned out exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a man sent to seek him at a certain place; it turned out exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 每為人占筮，小大必中。

translations.literal: Whenever he divined for others, great or small, he always hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he divined for others, great or small, he always hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 但用爻辭、彖象以辯吉兇，《易》占之屬，都不經口。

translations.literal: But he used only the line texts and the judgment images to distinguish fortune and misfortune; divination of the Changes sort he never spoke from his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: But he used only the line texts and the judgment images to distinguish fortune and misfortune; divination of the Changes sort he never spoke from his mouth.

sentences.zh: 會本貧生，無僕隸，初任助教之日，恒乘驢上下。

translations.literal: Hui was originally a poor student with no servants; in his first days as adjunct he always rode a donkey up and down.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was originally a poor student with no servants; in his first days as adjunct he always rode a donkey up and down.

sentences.zh: 且其職事處多，每須經歷，及其退食，非晚不歸。

translations.literal: Moreover his duties lay in many places and he had to pass through them constantly; when he left office for the day he did not return until late.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his duties lay in many places and he had to pass through them constantly; when he left office for the day he did not return until late.

sentences.zh: 曾夜出城東門，鐘漏已盡，會唯獨乘驢。

translations.literal: Once at night he went out the eastern gate; the clepsydra had already run out and Hui rode his donkey alone.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night he went out the eastern gate; the clepsydra had already run out and Hui rode his donkey alone.

sentences.zh: 忽有二人，一人牽頭，一人隨後，有似相助，其回動輕漂，有異生人。

translations.literal: Suddenly there were two men—one leading the head, one following behind—as if helping; their turning and movement were light and drifting, unlike living men.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly there were two men—one leading the head, one following behind—as if helping; their turning and movement were light and drifting, unlike living men.

sentences.zh: 漸漸失路，不由本道。

translations.literal: Gradually they lost the road and did not follow the original path.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually they lost the road and did not follow the original path.

sentences.zh: 會心甚怪之，遂誦《易經》上篇。

translations.literal: Hui thought it very strange and so recited the upper part of the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Hui thought it very strange and so recited the upper part of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 一卷不盡，前後二人，忽然離散。

translations.literal: Before one scroll was finished the two men before and behind suddenly scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Before one scroll was finished the two men before and behind suddenly scattered.

sentences.zh: 會亦不覺墮驢，因爾迷悶，至明始覺。

translations.literal: Hui also did not notice he had fallen from the donkey and so grew dizzy; only at dawn did he come to.
translations.idiomatic: Hui also did not notice he had fallen from the donkey and grew dizzy; only at dawn did he come to.

sentences.zh: 方知墮驢之處，乃是郭外，才去家數里。

translations.literal: Then he knew the place where he had fallen from the donkey was outside the city wall, only a few li from home.
translations.idiomatic: Then he knew the place where he had fallen from the donkey was outside the city wall, only a few li from home.

sentences.zh: 有一子，字子襲，聰敏精勤，幼有成人之量。

translations.literal: He had one son, styled Zixi, clever, keen, and diligent in youth, with the measure of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son, styled Zixi, clever, keen, and diligent in youth, with the measure of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 不幸先亡，臨送者為其傷慟，會唯一哭而罷，時人尚其達命。

translations.literal: Unfortunately he died first; those who escorted him wept in grief for him, but Hui wept only once and stopped—men of the time admired his acceptance of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Unfortunately he died first; those who escorted him wept in grief, but Hui wept only once and stopped—men of the time admired his acceptance of fate.

sentences.zh: 武平年，自府還第，在路無故馬倒，遂不得語，因爾暴亡，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the Wuping years, returning from his office to his residence, on the road for no reason his horse fell; he could not speak and so died suddenly, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuping years, returning from his office to his residence, on the road for no reason his horse fell; he could not speak and died suddenly, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 註《易》一部，行於世。

translations.literal: He annotated one work on the Changes, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated one work on the Changes, which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 會生平畏馬，位望所至，不得不乘，果以此終。

translations.literal: All his life Hui feared horses; the rank and eminence he reached forced him to ride, and in the end it was by this that he perished.
translations.idiomatic: All his life Hui feared horses; the rank and eminence he reached forced him to ride, and in the end it was by this that he perished.

sentences.zh: 張思伯，河間樂城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sibai was a man of Yuecheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sibai was a man of Yuecheng in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 善說《左氏傳》，為馬敬德之次。

translations.literal: Skilled at expounding Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, he stood second to Ma Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at expounding Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, he stood second to Ma Jingde.

sentences.zh: 撰《刊例》十卷，行於時，亦治《毛詩》章句，以二經教齊安王廓。

translations.literal: He compiled ten juan of Exemplary Precedents for Publication, which circulated in his day; he also worked through the Mao version of the Odes in chapter-and-commentary form, and with these two classics instructed Prince of Qi'an, Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ten juan of Exemplary Precedents for Publication, which circulated in his day; he also worked through the Mao version of the Odes in chapter-and-commentary form, and with these two classics instructed Prince of Qi'an, Kuo.

sentences.zh: 武平初，國子博士。

translations.literal: At the start of Wuping he was a doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Wuping he was a doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 張雕，中山北平人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Diao was a man of Pingbei in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Diao came from Pingbei in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 家世貧賤，而慷慨有志節，雅好古學。

translations.literal: His family had been poor and lowly, yet he was generous and possessed resolve; he loved antiquity and classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: His house was poor and low, yet he was open-handed and full of resolve, with a deep love for antiquity and the old learning.

sentences.zh: 精力絕人，負篋從師，不遠千里。

translations.literal: His strength was beyond other men; he carried a book-chest and followed teachers, not shrinking from a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: His strength was beyond other men; he shouldered a book-chest and followed teachers a thousand li without flinching.

sentences.zh: 遍通《五經》，尤明《三傳》，弟子遠方就業者以百數，諸儒服其強辨。

translations.literal: He mastered the Five Classics throughout, and was especially clear in the Three Commentaries; students who came from afar to study under him numbered in the hundreds, and the ru scholars submitted to his force in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics throughout and was especially clear in the Three Commentaries; students who came from afar to study under him numbered in the hundreds, and the ru scholars bowed to his force in debate.

sentences.zh: 魏末，以明經召入霸府，高祖令與諸子講讀。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he was summoned into the hegemon's office on account of his mastery of the classics; Gaozu ordered him to lecture and read with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was summoned into the hegemon's office for his mastery of the classics; Gaozu ordered him to lecture and read with the princes.

sentences.zh: 起家殄寇將軍，稍遷太尉長流參軍、定州主簿。

translations.literal: He began his career as General Who Extinguishes Bandits, and was gradually promoted to long-flow aide in the Grand Marshal's office and chief clerk of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as General Who Extinguishes Bandits, then rose by degrees to long-flow aide in the Grand Marshal's office and chief clerk of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 從世宗赴幷，除常山府長流參軍。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong to Bing and was made long-flow aide in the Prince of Changshan's establishment office.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong to Bing and was made long-flow aide in the Prince of Changshan's establishment office.

sentences.zh: 天保中，為永安王府參軍事。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was a staff officer in the Prince of Yong'an's establishment office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he served as staff officer in the Prince of Yong'an's establishment office.

sentences.zh: 顯祖崩於晉陽，擢兼祠部郎中，典喪事，從梓宮還鄴。

translations.literal: When Xianzu died at Jinyang, Diao was promoted to acting director in the Ministry of Rites and oversaw the mourning; he accompanied the bier back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu died at Jinyang, Diao was promoted to acting director in the Ministry of Rites to oversee the mourning and accompanied the bier back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，除國子博士。

translations.literal: At the start of Qianming he was made doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qianming he was made doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 遷平原太守，坐贓賄失官。

translations.literal: He was moved to governor of Pingyuan and lost his post on a charge of bribery.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to governor of Pingyuan and lost his post on a charge of bribery.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，以舊恩除通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, on account of old favor he was made attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, old favor won him the post of attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.

sentences.zh: 瑯邪王儼求博士精儒學，有司以雕應選，時號得人。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Yan sought a doctor steeped in Confucian learning; the authorities nominated Diao, and at the time people said the right man had been found.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Yan wanted a doctor steeped in Confucian learning; the authorities nominated Diao, and the talk of the time said the right man had been found.

sentences.zh: 尋為涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made inspector of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made inspector of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜散騎常侍，復為儼講。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed attendant of irregular cavalry and again lectured for Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed attendant of irregular cavalry and again lectured for Yan.

sentences.zh: 值帝侍講馬敬德卒，乃入授經書。

translations.literal: It happened that Ma Jingde, the emperor's lecturer-in-attendance, died; Diao then entered to transmit the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Jingde, the emperor's lecturer-in-attendance, died, Diao entered to transmit the classics in his place.

sentences.zh: 帝甚重之，以為侍讀，與張景仁並被尊禮，同入華光殿，共讀《春秋》。

translations.literal: The emperor valued him highly, made him a reader-in-attendance, and with Zhang Jingren he was alike honored; together they entered the Hall of Splendid Light to read the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued him highly, made him reader-in-attendance, and with Zhang Jingren he shared equal honor; together they entered the Hall of Splendid Light to read the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 加國子祭酒，假儀同三司，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: He was further made Director of the Imperial University, given acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Director of the Imperial University, given acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall.

sentences.zh: 胡人何洪珍大蒙主上親寵，與張景仁結為婚媾。

translations.literal: The Hu man He Hongzhen had won the ruler's intimate favor; he and Zhang Jingren became kin by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu man He Hongzhen had won the ruler's intimate favor; he and Zhang Jingren bound their houses by marriage.

sentences.zh: 雕以景仁宗室，自託於洪珍，傾心相禮，情好日密，公私之事，雕常為其指南。

translations.literal: Because Jingren was of the imperial clan, Diao attached himself to Hongzhen and poured out his heart in courtesy; day by day their affection grew close, and in public and private affairs Diao often served as his guide.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jingren was of the imperial clan, Diao attached himself to Hongzhen and poured out his heart in courtesy; day by day their affection grew close, and in public and private affairs Diao often served as his guide.

sentences.zh: 時穆提婆、韓長鸞與洪珍同侍帷幄，知雕為洪珍謀主，甚忌惡之。

translations.literal: At that time Mutipo, Han Changluan, and Hongzhen alike attended within the curtain; knowing Diao was Hongzhen's chief strategist, they deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mutipo, Han Changluan, and Hongzhen alike attended within the curtain; knowing Diao was Hongzhen's chief strategist, they hated him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 洪珍又奏雕監國史。

translations.literal: Hongzhen also memorialized that Diao should supervise the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhen also memorialized that Diao should supervise the national history.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，加開府，奏度支事，大被委任，言多見從。

translations.literal: Soon he was made attendant-in-chief, given the grand marshal's office, and put in charge of revenue affairs; he was greatly entrusted, and his words were often followed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant-in-chief, given the grand marshal's office, and put in charge of revenue affairs; he was greatly entrusted, and his words were often followed.

sentences.zh: 特勑奏事不趨，呼為博士。

translations.literal: A special edict allowed him to report without hurrying; he was called the Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict allowed him to report without hurrying; the court called him the Doctor.

sentences.zh: 雕自以出於微賤，致位大臣，勵精在公，有匪躬之節，欲立功效以報朝恩。

translations.literal: Diao, knowing he had risen from the humblest origins to the rank of great minister, strove in public affairs with a spirit that would not spare his own body, wishing to establish merit and repay the court's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Diao, knowing he had risen from the humblest origins to great minister, strove in public affairs with a spirit that would not spare his own body, wishing to establish merit and repay the court's grace.

sentences.zh: 論議抑揚，無所回避。

translations.literal: In debate he would raise or lower a point without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he would raise or lower a point without evasion.

sentences.zh: 宮掖不急之費，大存減省，左右縱恣之徒，必加禁約，數譏切寵要，獻替帷扆。

translations.literal: Unnecessary expenses within the palace were sharply reduced; those about him who indulged in license were strictly restrained; he repeatedly rebuked the favored and powerful and offered counsel at the throne's side.
translations.idiomatic: Unnecessary expenses within the palace were sharply cut; those about him who indulged in license were strictly restrained; he repeatedly rebuked the favored and powerful and offered counsel at the throne's side.

sentences.zh: 上亦深倚仗之，方委以朝政。

translations.literal: The ruler also leaned on him deeply and was about to entrust him with court government.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler also leaned on him deeply and was about to entrust him with the government of the court.

sentences.zh: 雕便以澄清為己任，意氣甚高。

translations.literal: Diao then took clarification as his own charge, and his spirit ran very high.
translations.idiomatic: Diao then took clarification as his own charge, and his spirit ran very high.

sentences.zh: 嘗在朝堂謂鄭子信曰：「向入省中，見賢家唐令處分極無所以，若作數行兵帳，雕不如邕，若致主堯舜，身居稷、契，則邕不如我。

translations.literal: Once in the court hall he said to Zheng Zixin: "When I went into the Secretariat just now, I saw your esteemed family's Tang Ling's dispositions were utterly without reason. If it were making a few lines of military registers, Diao would not match Yong; if it were bringing the ruler to Yao and Shun and oneself occupying the stations of Hou Ji and Qi, then Yong would not match me."
translations.idiomatic: Once in the court hall he said to Zheng Zixin, "When I went into the Secretariat just now, I saw your esteemed family's Tang Ling's dispositions were utterly without reason. If it were making a few lines of military registers, Diao would not match Yong; if it were bringing the ruler to Yao and Shun and oneself occupying the stations of Hou Ji and Qi, then Yong would not match me."

sentences.zh: 」其矜誕如此。

translations.literal: His arrogance and extravagance were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance and extravagance ran to such a pitch.

sentences.zh: 長鸞等慮其干政不已，陰圖之。

translations.literal: Changluan and the rest feared he would not cease meddling in government and secretly plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan and the rest feared he would not cease meddling in government and plotted against him in secret.

sentences.zh: 會雕與侍中崔季舒等諫帝幸晉陽，長鸞因譖之，故俱誅死。

translations.literal: It happened that Diao, together with the attendant-in-chief Cui Jishu and others, remonstrated against the emperor's journey to Jinyang; Changluan therefore slandered them, and so all were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Diao, together with attendant-in-chief Cui Jishu and others, remonstrated against the emperor's journey to Jinyang; Changluan slandered them, and so all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，帝令段孝言詰之。

translations.literal: At the execution the emperor ordered Duan Xiaoyan to question him.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution the emperor ordered Duan Xiaoyan to question him.

sentences.zh: 雕致對曰：「臣起自諸生，謬被抽擢，接事累世，常蒙恩遇，位至開府侍中，光寵隆洽。

translations.literal: Diao replied: "Your servant rose from among the ru scholars, was wrongly drawn up and promoted, received office through successive reigns, and constantly enjoyed grace; I reached grand marshal's office and attendant-in-chief, with glory and favor heaped upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Diao replied, "Your servant rose from among the ru scholars, was wrongly drawn up and promoted, received office through successive reigns, and constantly enjoyed grace; I reached grand marshal's office and attendant-in-chief, with glory and favor heaped upon me.

sentences.zh: 每思塵露，微益山海。

translations.literal: Each time I thought how dust and dew might in the smallest measure repay mountains and seas.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I thought how dust and dew might in the smallest measure repay mountains and seas.

sentences.zh: 今者之諫，臣實首謀，意善功惡，無所逃死。

translations.literal: In today's remonstrance I was truly the chief plotter; the intent was good but the outcome evil, and there is no escaping death.
translations.idiomatic: In today's remonstrance I was truly the chief plotter; the intent was good but the outcome evil, and there is no escaping death.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下珍愛金玉，開發神明，數引賈誼之倫，論說治道，令聽覽之間，無所擁蔽，則臣雖死之日，猶生之年。

translations.literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty will treasure gold and jade, open and develop your divine clarity, often summon men of Jia Yi's sort to discuss the way of governance, so that between what you hear and behold nothing is blocked—and then though the day of my death come, it will be as a day of life."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty will treasure gold and jade, open and develop your divine clarity, often summon men of Jia Yi's sort to discuss the way of governance, so that between what you hear and behold nothing is blocked—and then though the day of my death come, it will be as a day of life."

sentences.zh: 」歔欷流涕，俯而就戮，侍衛左右莫不憐而壯之。

translations.literal: He sobbed with tears streaming, bowed his head and went to the blade; the guards on either side all pitied him and yet found him splendid.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed with tears streaming, bowed his head and went to the blade; the guards on either side all pitied him and yet found him splendid.

sentences.zh: 時年五十五。

translations.literal: He was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 子德沖等徙於北邊。

translations.literal: His son Dechong and the rest were banished to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dechong and the rest were banished to the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 南安之反，德沖及弟德揭俱死。

translations.literal: When Nan'an rebelled, Dechong and his younger brother Dejie both died.
translations.idiomatic: When Nan'an rebelled, Dechong and his younger brother Dejie both died.

sentences.zh: 德沖和謹謙讓，善於人倫，聰敏好學，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: Dechong was harmonious, careful, and yielding, skilled in human relations, clever and fond of learning, and had dipped into letters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Dechong was harmonious, careful, and yielding, skilled in human relations, clever and fond of learning, and had dipped into letters and histories.

sentences.zh: 以帝師之子，早見旌擢。

translations.literal: As the son of the emperor's teacher, he was early singled out for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of the emperor's teacher, he was early singled out for promotion.

sentences.zh: 歷員外散騎侍郎、太師府掾，入為中書舍人，隨例待詔。

translations.literal: He passed through attendant of irregular cavalry outside the regular roster and recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment office, then entered as gentleman of the Secretariat and, by precedent, was kept on call.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through attendant of irregular cavalry outside the regular roster and recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment office, then entered as gentleman of the Secretariat and, by precedent, was kept on call.

sentences.zh: 其父之戮也，德沖在殿庭執事，目見冤酷，號哭殞絕於地，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: At his father's execution Dechong was on duty in the palace hall; he saw the cruel injustice with his own eyes, wailed until he collapsed senseless on the ground, and only after long while came back to himself.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's execution Dechong was on duty in the palace hall; he saw the cruel injustice with his own eyes, wailed until he collapsed senseless on the ground, and only after a long while came back to himself.

sentences.zh: 孫靈暉，長樂武強人也。

translations.literal: Sun Linghui was a man of Wuqiang in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Linghui came from Wuqiang in Changle.

sentences.zh: 魏大儒秘書監惠蔚，靈暉之族曾王父也。

translations.literal: Huiwei, the great ru of Wei and director of the Secretariat, was Linghui's great-great-grandfather on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei, the great ru of Wei and director of the Secretariat, was Linghui's great-great-grandfather on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 靈暉少明敏，有器度。

translations.literal: Linghui from youth was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Linghui from youth was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚一子早卒，其家書籍多在焉。

translations.literal: Huiwei's one son had died early; most of the family's books were there.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei's one son had died early; most of the family's books were there.

sentences.zh: 靈暉年七歲，便好學，日誦數千言，唯尋討惠蔚手錄章疏，不求師友。

translations.literal: At seven sui Linghui already loved learning; each day he recited several thousand words, seeking out only the chapter summaries Huiwei had copied by hand, and not asking teachers or friends.
translations.idiomatic: At seven sui Linghui already loved learning; each day he recited several thousand words, seeking out only the chapter summaries Huiwei had copied by hand, and not asking teachers or friends.

sentences.zh: 《三禮》及《三傳》皆通宗旨，始就鮑季詳、熊安生質問疑滯，其所發明，熊、鮑無以異也。

translations.literal: The Three Rites and the Three Commentaries he all mastered in their main purport; when he first went to Bao Jixiang and Xiong Ansheng to question what puzzled him, what he brought to light left Xiong and Bao with nothing to differ over.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rites and the Three Commentaries he mastered in their main purport; when he first went to Bao Jixiang and Xiong Ansheng to question what puzzled him, what he brought to light left Xiong and Bao with nothing to differ over.

sentences.zh: 舉冀州刺史秀才，射策高第，授員外將軍。

translations.literal: He was nominated as the Ji province's xiucai; in the archery-and-writing examination he took a high place and was given the rank of acting general outside the regular roster.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated as the Ji province's xiucai; in the archery-and-writing examination he took a high place and was given the rank of acting general outside the regular roster.

sentences.zh: 後以儒術甄明，擢授太學博士。

translations.literal: Later, because his Confucian learning was clear and distinguished, he was promoted and appointed doctor of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his Confucian learning was clear and distinguished, he was promoted and appointed doctor of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷北徐州治中，轉潼郡太守。

translations.literal: He was moved to supervisory aide of North Xuzhou and then transferred to governor of Tong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to supervisory aide of North Xuzhou and then transferred to governor of Tong commandery.

sentences.zh: 天統中，敕令朝臣推舉可為南陽王綽師者，吏部尚書尉瑾表薦之，征為國子博士，授南陽王經。

translations.literal: In the Tiantong era an edict ordered court ministers to recommend who might serve as teacher to Prince of Nanyang, Chuo; the Minister of Personnel Yu Jin memorialized him; he was summoned as doctor of the Imperial University and transmitted the classics to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiantong era an edict ordered court ministers to recommend who might serve as teacher to Prince of Nanyang, Chuo; the Minister of Personnel Yu Jin memorialized him; he was summoned as doctor of the Imperial University and transmitted the classics to the prince.

sentences.zh: 王雖不好文學，亦甚相敬重，啟除其府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Though the prince did not love letters, he still greatly respected Linghui and memorialized to make him consulting aide in the prince's establishment office.
translations.idiomatic: Though the prince did not love letters, he still greatly respected Linghui and memorialized to make him consulting aide in the prince's establishment office.

sentences.zh: 綽除定州刺史，仍隨之鎮。

translations.literal: When Chuo was made inspector of Ding province, Linghui still followed him to the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo was made inspector of Ding province, Linghui still followed him to the garrison.

sentences.zh: 綽所為猖蹶，靈暉唯默默憂悴，不能諫止。

translations.literal: What Chuo did was reckless and violent; Linghui could only grieve in silence and could not remonstrate and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: What Chuo did was reckless and violent; Linghui could only grieve in silence and could not remonstrate and stop him.

sentences.zh: 綽欲以管記馬子結為諮議參軍，乃表請轉靈暉為王師，以子結為諮議。

translations.literal: Chuo wished to make his recorder Ma Zijie consulting aide; he therefore memorialized asking to transfer Linghui to prince's teacher and make Zijie consulting aide.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo wished to make his recorder Ma Zijie consulting aide; he therefore memorialized asking to transfer Linghui to prince's teacher and make Zijie consulting aide.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以王師三品，啟奏不合。

translations.literal: The court held that prince's teacher was third rank and that such a memorial did not accord with regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that prince's teacher was third rank and that such a memorial did not accord with regulations.

sentences.zh: 後主於啟下手答，云「但用之」，仍手報南陽書，並依所奏。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler wrote a reply beneath the memorial: "Simply use him," and still wrote in his own hand to the Prince of Nanyang; both followed what had been memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler wrote a reply beneath the memorial: "Simply use him," and still wrote in his own hand to the Prince of Nanyang; both followed what had been memorialized.

sentences.zh: 儒者甚以為榮。

translations.literal: The ru scholars greatly took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: The ru scholars greatly took it as glory.

sentences.zh: 綽除大將軍，靈暉以王師領大將軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Chuo was made grand marshal, Linghui as prince's teacher concurrently held the post of chief of staff in the grand marshal's establishment office.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo was made grand marshal, Linghui as prince's teacher concurrently held the post of chief of staff in the grand marshal's establishment office.

sentences.zh: 綽誅，停廢。

translations.literal: When Chuo was executed, Linghui was suspended and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo was executed, Linghui was suspended and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 從綽死後，每至七日及百日終，靈暉恒為綽請僧設齋，轉經行道。

translations.literal: After Chuo's death, on each seventh day and at the end of the hundredth day Linghui always begged monks on Chuo's behalf and set out offerings, turning the sutras and walking the rite.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuo's death, on each seventh day and at the end of the hundredth day Linghui always begged monks on Chuo's behalf and set out offerings, turning the sutras and walking the rite.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years after Qi's fall he died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after Qi's fall he died.

sentences.zh: 子萬壽，聰識機警，博涉群書，《禮傳》俱通大議，有辭藻，尤甚詩詠。

translations.literal: His son Wanshou was clever, perceptive, and quick; he ranged widely through many books, mastered the main purport of both Rites and Commentaries, had literary polish, and was especially given to poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wanshou was clever, perceptive, and quick; he ranged widely through many books, mastered the main purport of both Rites and Commentaries, had literary polish, and was especially given to poetry.

sentences.zh: 齊末，陽休之辟為開府行參軍。

translations.literal: Late in Qi, Yang Xiuzhi recruited him as traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qi, Yang Xiuzhi recruited him as traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government.

sentences.zh: 隋奉朝請、滕王文學、豫章長史。

translations.literal: Under Sui he was court gentleman attendant, literary scholar to the Prince of Teng, and chief administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he was court gentleman attendant, literary scholar to the Prince of Teng, and chief administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 卒於大理司直。

translations.literal: He died in the post of direct judge in the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the post of direct judge in the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 馬子結者，其先扶風人也。

translations.literal: Ma Zijie—his forebears were men of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zijie—his forebears were men of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 世居涼土，太和中入洛。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt in the Liang lands; in the Taihe era they entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they dwelt in the Liang lands; in the Taihe era they entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父祖俱清官。

translations.literal: Father and grandfathers alike held clean offices.
translations.idiomatic: Father and grandfathers alike held clean offices.

sentences.zh: 子結兄弟三人，皆涉文學。

translations.literal: The three brothers Zijie, Zilian, and Zishang were all versed in letters.
translations.idiomatic: The three brothers Zijie, Zilian, and Zishang were all versed in letters.

sentences.zh: 陽休之牧西兗，子廉、子尚、子結與諸朝士各有詩言贈，陽總為一篇酬答，卽詩云「三馬俱白眉」者也。

translations.literal: When Yang Xiuzhi governed West Yan, Zilian, Zishang, Zijie, and the other court gentlemen each had a poem of farewell; Yang gathered them into one piece in reply—that is the poem that says "the three Ma all have white brows."
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xiuzhi governed West Yan, Zilian, Zishang, Zijie, and the other court gentlemen each had a poem of farewell; Yang gathered them into one piece in reply—that is the poem that says "the three Ma all have white brows."

sentences.zh: 子結以開府行參軍擢為南陽王管記，隨綽定州。

translations.literal: Zijie was promoted from traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government to recorder for Prince of Nanyang Chuo and followed Chuo to Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: Zijie was promoted from traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government to recorder for Prince of Nanyang Chuo and followed Chuo to Ding province.

sentences.zh: 綽每出遊獵，必令子結走馬從禽。

translations.literal: Whenever Chuo went out to tour and hunt, he always made Zijie run his horse alongside the game.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chuo went out to tour and hunt, he always made Zijie run his horse alongside the game.

sentences.zh: 子結旣儒緩，衣垂帽落，或噭或啼，令騎驅之，非墜馬不止，綽以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Zijie was by nature ru-soft; his robes trailed and his hat slipped, and he would cry out or weep; Chuo had the riders drive him on and would not stop until Zijie fell from his horse—Chuo took it for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Zijie was by nature ru-soft; his robes trailed and his hat slipped, and he would cry out or weep; Chuo had the riders drive him on and would not stop until Zijie fell from his horse—Chuo took it for sport.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見親狎，啟為諮議云。

translations.literal: By this he gradually grew intimate; Chuo memorialized to make him consulting aide.
translations.idiomatic: By this he gradually grew intimate; Chuo memorialized to make him consulting aide.

sentences.zh: 石曜，字白曜，中山安喜人，亦以儒學進。

translations.literal: Shi Yao, styled Baiyao, was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan; he too advanced through Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yao, styled Baiyao, came from Anxi in Zhongshan; he too advanced through Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 居官至清儉。

translations.literal: In office he reached the end as pure and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: In office he reached the end as pure and frugal.

sentences.zh: 武平中黎陽郡守，值斛律武都出為兗州刺史，武都卽丞相咸陽王世子，皇后之兄，性甚貪暴。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was governor of Liyang commandery; it happened that Hulü Wudu went out as inspector of Yan province—Wudu was the heir of the Chancellor, Prince of Xianyang, and the empress's elder brother, and by nature was very greedy and violent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he was governor of Liyang commandery; it happened that Hulü Wudu went out as inspector of Yan province—Wudu was the heir of the Chancellor, Prince of Xianyang, and the empress's elder brother, and by nature was very greedy and violent.

sentences.zh: 先過衛縣，令丞以下聚斂絹數千疋以遺之。

translations.literal: He had first passed through Wei county; the magistrate, assistant, and those below had levied several thousand bolts of silk as gifts to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had first passed through Wei county; the magistrate, assistant, and those below had levied several thousand bolts of silk as gifts to him.

sentences.zh: 及至黎陽，令左右諷動曜及郡治下縣官。

translations.literal: When he reached Liyang he had those at his side hint and stir up Yao and the county officials under the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Liyang he had those at his side hint and stir up Yao and the county officials under the commandery.

sentences.zh: 曜手持一縑而謂武都曰：「此是老石機杼，聊以奉贈。

translations.literal: Yao held a single bolt of silk in his hand and said to Wudu: "This is old Shi's loom-cloth; I offer it merely as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yao held a single bolt of silk in his hand and said to Wudu, "This is old Shi's loom-cloth; I offer it merely as a gift.

sentences.zh: 自此來並須出於吏民，吏民之物，一毫不敢輒犯。

translations.literal: Beyond this, everything must come from clerks and people; of what belongs to clerks and people, not a hair's breadth may be rashly touched."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, everything must come from clerks and people; of what belongs to clerks and people, not a hair's breadth may be rashly touched."

sentences.zh: 」武都亦知曜清素純儒，笑而不責。

translations.literal: Wudu also knew Yao was pure, plain, and a pure ru; he laughed and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudu also knew Yao was pure, plain, and a pure ru; he laughed and did not blame him.

sentences.zh: 著《石子》十卷，言甚淺俗。

translations.literal: He authored ten juan of Master Shi, whose words were very shallow and vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: He authored ten juan of Master Shi, whose words were very shallow and vulgar.

sentences.zh: 後終於譙州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he ended his days as inspector of Qiao province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he ended his days as inspector of Qiao province.

sentences.zh: 此外行事史闕焉。

translations.literal: Beyond this, their deeds in the histories are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, their deeds in the histories are lacking.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：大道旣隱，名教是遵，以斯建國，以此立身。

translations.literal: Praise: The Great Way has already been hidden; name and teaching are what one follows—with these a state is built, with these a person stands.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: The Great Way has already been hidden; name and teaching are what one follows—with these a state is built, with these a person stands.

sentences.zh: 帝圖雜霸，儒風未純，何以不墜，弘之在人。

translations.literal: The imperial design mixed with hegemony; the ru wind was not yet pure—how could it not fall? To keep it from falling was to enlarge it in men.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial design mixed with hegemony; the ru wind was not yet pure—how could it not fall? To keep it from falling was to enlarge it in men.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
